text: The accounting equation is stated as:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Assets = Capital - Liabilities|Assets = Liabilities + Capital|Assets + Capital = Liabilities|Capital = Assets + Liabilities
explanation: Assets equal the sum of outside claims (liabilities) and the owner's claims (capital).

text: Recording a transaction in the journal for the first time is called:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Journalising|Ledgerising|Balancing off|Posting
explanation: The journal is the book of original entry.

text: When cash is received from a customer on account the entry is:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Debit Cash and Credit the customer's account|Debit the customer's account and Credit Cash|Debit Cash and Credit Sales|Debit Sales and Credit Cash
explanation: Cash (asset) increases with a debit and the debtor's claim decreases with a credit.

text: Every transaction affects at least two accounts in equal amounts. This is the:
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: This is the dual aspect concept of double entry book keeping.

text: State the dual aspect concept of accounting.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Every transaction has two equal and opposite effects so two entries (a debit and a credit) are recorded.

text: The ledger is called the book of:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Cash entry|Original entry|Final entry|Subsidiary entry only
explanation: The journal records transactions first and the ledger (final entry) groups them by account.

text: The trial balance is prepared mainly to check the:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Solvency of the business|Efficiency of the staff|Profitability of the business|Arithmetic accuracy of ledger posting
explanation: Equality of total debits and credits detects one sided and amount errors.

text: A cash account showing a credit balance in the trial balance indicates:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: An overdrawn position|A credit sale|An arithmetical error only|A cash shortage
explanation: When the bank pays more than the business deposits the cash book balance becomes negative.

text: The trial balance will NOT detect an error of omission. This statement is:
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: When a transaction is completely left out both sides stay equal so the trial balance agrees.

text: List any four errors that are not disclosed by the trial balance.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Errors of omission; errors of commission; errors of principle; and compensating errors.

text: The statement that shows the profit earned from trading is the:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Balance Sheet|Cash Flow Statement|Profit and Loss Account|Trading Account
explanation: The trading account computes gross profit from sales and cost of goods sold.

text: Gross profit is calculated as:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Sales minus drawings|Net sales minus all expenses|Net sales minus cost of goods sold|Revenue plus capital
explanation: Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases + direct expenses - closing stock.

text: Closing stock is shown:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Only in the Balance Sheet|Only in the Trading Account|On the credit side of the Trading Account and as current asset in the Balance Sheet|Only in the Profit and Loss Account
explanation: It is valued for the trading account and reported as a current asset.

text: A current liability such as a creditor is shown on the:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Debit side of the Trading Account|Credit side of the P and L Account only|Assets side of the Balance Sheet|Liabilities side of the Balance Sheet
explanation: Liabilities and capital appear on the liabilities side of the balance sheet.

text: Distinguish between gross profit and net profit.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Gross profit is sales minus cost of goods sold; net profit is gross profit minus operating expenses plus non operating incomes.

text: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared to reconcile:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Sales with debtors|Assets with liabilities|The cash book balance with the pass book balance|The trial balance with the balance sheet
explanation: It explains differences such as cheques not presented and bank charges not recorded.

text: A cheque deposited and recorded in the cash book but not yet cleared by the bank is in the BRS:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Deducted from the pass book balance|Added to the pass book balance|Ignored completely|Debited in the pass book
explanation: The pass book has not yet received the credit so it is added to reach the cash book figure.

text: Depreciation is charged because of:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Physical wear and tear only|Obsolescence only|The passage of time; wear and tear; and obsolescence|Capital loss only
explanation: The service potential of a fixed asset falls for all three reasons.

text: Under the straight line method the depreciation charge each year is the same on the original cost.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: A fixed percentage of the original cost is charged until the asset is fully depreciated.

text: State any three methods of providing depreciation.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Straight line method; diminishing balance method; and units of production method.

text: A valid contract requires:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Offer and acceptance only|Free consent; lawful consideration; competent parties; and a lawful object|A written document only|Stamp paper only
explanation: All the essentials under the Indian Contract Act 1872 must be present together.

text: Coercion in the Indian Contract Act means:
subject: Commercial Law
options: A written notice|An expression of two or more meanings|Obtaining consent by unlawful pressure or threat|A casual promise
explanation: Coercion vitiates free consent and makes the contract voidable.

text: A contract may come to an end by performance; mutual agreement; or lapse of time. This statement is:
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: These are the standard modes of discharge of a contract.

text: List the essentials of a valid contract under the Indian Contract Act.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: Offer and acceptance; intention to create legal relation; competent parties; free consent; lawful consideration; lawful object; and it must not be declared void.

text: In the absence of a special agreement risk normally follows:
subject: Commercial Law
subtopic: Goods Risk and Transfer of Property
options: Payment|The invoice date|Delivery|Title
explanation: Where property passes the loss by destruction falls on the owner even before delivery.

text: A sale of goods is complete when:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Property in the goods passes from the seller to the buyer|The goods reach the buyer|The invoice is issued|The full price is paid
explanation: Transfer of property is the defining moment of sale.

text: Goods under the Sale of Goods Act include:
subject: Commercial Law
subtopic: Goods Risk and Transfer of Property
options: Shares in a company|Money only|All movable property other than money and actionable claims|Land and buildings
explanation: The Act covers movables such as stock and growing crops but not money or intangible claims.

text: In a sale on approval the buyer may test the goods and return them if not satisfied. This statement is:
subject: Commercial Law
subtopic: Goods Risk and Transfer of Property
explanation: Property passes only when the buyer approves or keeps the goods beyond the allowed time.

text: State the conditions implied under the Sale of Goods Act.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: Seller's title; merchantable quality; fitness for the particular purpose; and correspondence with description.

text: A cheque is a negotiable instrument under:
subject: Commercial Law
options: The Negotiable Instruments Act|The Sales Tax Act|The Companies Act|The Indian Contract Act
explanation: The Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 governs promissory notes; bills of exchange; and cheques.

text: A bill of exchange is a written instruction:
subject: Commercial Law
options: From the buyer to the seller|From the bank to the customer only|From the government to the citizen|From the drawer to the drawee to pay a certain sum to the order of a person
explanation: It involves three parties: the drawer; the drawee; and the payee.

text: A promissory note is made and signed by the debtor who promises to pay. This statement is:
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: The maker of a note is the principal debtor and only two parties are involved.

text: Distinguish between a promissory note and a bill of exchange.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: A note is a written promise by the maker to pay and has two parties; a bill is a written order from drawer to drawee and has three parties; a note needs no acceptance.

text: The Consumer Protection Act 2019 replaced the:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Contract Act of 1872|Sale of Goods Act of 1930|Companies Act of 2013|Act of 1986
explanation: The 2019 Act introduced e commerce protection and a three level commission structure.

text: A dissatisfied consumer may approach the:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Appropriate Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission|Police station only|A private arbitration tribunal only|Supreme Court only
explanation: Complaints go to the district; state; or national commission depending on the value of the claim.

text: Deficiency in service means any fault or lack in the quality or standard of service. This statement is:
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: It covers poor quality; delay; and non performance of promised services.

text: The basic consumer rights include the right to safety; information; choice; and redressal. This statement is:
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: The Act also lists the right to be heard and consumer education.

text: List any four rights of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: Right to safety; right to be informed; right to choose; right to redressal; right to be heard; and consumer education.

text: The probability of an impossible event is:
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: An impossible event never occurs so its probability is zero.

text: The sum of the probabilities of all outcomes of a random experiment is:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Undefined|0|1|Greater than 1
explanation: All possible outcomes together are certain so their probabilities add to one.

text: The standard deviation is the square root of the:
subject: Business Mathematics
subtopic: Measures of Dispersion and Central Tendency
options: Median|Mode|Range|Variance
explanation: It expresses the average spread of data around the mean in the original units.

text: The mean of a grouped frequency distribution can be estimated by the step deviation method. This statement is:
subject: Business Mathematics
subtopic: Measures of Dispersion and Central Tendency
explanation: It is a shortcut of the assumed mean method that works on small coded deviations.

text: An index number expresses the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Quantity of goods produced|Absolute change in a single item|Relative change in a group of related variables|Only a single price
explanation: It measures percentage change of a group of prices; quantities; or values against a base period.

text: The simple aggregate method of constructing a price index is also called the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Geometric method|Arithmetic method|Weighted method|Fisher method
explanation: It divides the aggregate of current prices by the aggregate of base prices and multiplies by 100.

text: Fishers ideal index number is the geometric mean of the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Laspeyres and Paasche indices|Base year and current year prices|Quantity index and price index|Two aggregate indices
explanation: It satisfies the time reversal and factor reversal tests.

text: A consumer price index is mainly useful for measuring household inflation. This statement is:
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: It tracks price changes of a fixed basket of consumer goods and services.

text: The four components of a time series are:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Debit; credit; balance; and total|Input; output; stock; and flow|Trend; seasonal; cyclical; and irregular|Mean; median; mode; and range
explanation: Any observed value is modeled as a combination of these four forces.

text: The long term rising or falling movement in data is called the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Business cycle|Seasonal variation|Trend|Irregular variation
explanation: It is the secular movement that shows the general direction of the series.

text: Seasonal variation is a change within a year that repeats regularly. This statement is:
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: Examples are holiday shopping peaks and monsoon demand patterns.

text: The moving average method is used to estimate the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Irregular variation only|Random error only|Trend|Mode
explanation: Averaging over a window smooths seasonal and irregular fluctuations to reveal the trend.

text: In a linear programming problem the objective is to:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Compute a determinant|Balance the books of account|Maximize or minimize a linear function subject to linear constraints|Solve a quadratic equation
explanation: Both the objective function and the constraints must be linear.

text: The set of all feasible solutions of a linear programming problem is called the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Dual region|Objective region|Feasible region|Shadow region
explanation: It is the common area satisfying every constraint including non negativity.

text: The simplex method moves from one:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Center to the edge of the graph|Row to the next column|Random point to another random point|Corner point to an adjacent better corner point
explanation: An optimum of a linear program always lies at a vertex of the feasible region.

text: Slack variables are added to less than or equal to constraints to convert them into equations. This statement is:
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: They represent the unused portion of a scarce resource.

text: State the steps of the graphical method for a two variable linear programming problem.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: Plot each constraint line; shade the feasible region; evaluate the objective function at every corner point; and choose the corner that gives the best value.

text: According to the law of demand a rise in price causes the quantity demanded to fall. This statement is:
subject: Economics
explanation: The inverse relation holds when other determinants remain unchanged (ceteris paribus).

text: A shift of the demand curve (not a movement along it) is caused by:
subject: Economics
options: A change in consumer income|A change in the quantity demanded|A change in the price alone|A change in the own price of the good
explanation: Income; tastes; prices of related goods; expectations; and the number of buyers shift the curve.

text: When demand rises and supply stays the same the equilibrium price:
subject: Economics
options: Falls|Rises|Stays the same|Becomes zero
explanation: The demand curve shifts right and the intersection moves up along the supply curve.

text: The income method of computing national income adds up:
subject: Economics
options: Government debt|The factor incomes of all producers|Final consumer spending|Exports only
explanation: Wages; rent; interest; and profit are summed to get factor income at factor cost.

text: GNP at market prices equals GDP at factor cost plus net factor income from abroad plus:
subject: Economics
subtopic: GDP GNP and Per Capita Income
options: Indirect taxes minus subsidies|Subsidies minus indirect taxes|Depreciation|Interest on debt
explanation: Statistical adjustments convert factor cost into market prices.

text: Per capita income is national income divided by the population. This statement is:
subject: Economics
subtopic: GDP GNP and Per Capita Income
explanation: It is used to compare the average income and living standard across countries.

text: The output method computes national income as the sum of value added at each stage of production. This statement is:
subject: Economics
explanation: Adding value added avoids double counting of intermediate goods.

text: List three problems in the measurement of national income.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Double counting; non monetary transactions such as home work; and the underground economy of unrecorded activity.

text: The functions of money include:
subject: Economics
options: Only lending|Only payment of taxes|Only savings|Medium of exchange; store of value; and unit of account
explanation: These three are the classic functions recognized in monetary theory.

text: The central bank of India is the:
subject: Economics
options: State Bank of India|Reserve Bank of India|National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development|Union Bank of India
explanation: The RBI acts as banker to the government and to commercial banks.

text: The cash reserve ratio is the fraction of deposits that banks must keep with the RBI as cash. This statement is:
subject: Economics
explanation: Raising the CRR reduces the money banks can lend and tightens liquidity.

text: A country has a comparative advantage when it can produce a good at a:
subject: Economics
options: Higher absolute cost|Lower opportunity cost|Zero cost|Equal cost to others
explanation: Gains from trade arise from differences in opportunity costs not absolute costs.

text: The main advantage of free trade is:
subject: Economics
options: Higher tariffs on imports|Reduced competition|Protection of infant industries|Efficient allocation of resources and higher consumer welfare
explanation: Resources move to their most productive use and consumers get variety at lower prices.

text: The balance of payments is in equilibrium when the current account plus the capital account equals zero. This statement is:
subject: Economics
subtopic: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates
explanation: A deficit in one account is financed by a surplus in the other.

text: A depreciation of the rupee makes:
subject: Economics
subtopic: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates
options: International trade impossible|Indian exports cheaper for foreign buyers|Imports cheaper for Indians|Both exports and imports cheaper
explanation: Foreign buyers need fewer of their own currency units for the same rupee price.

text: If assets are 500000 and outside liabilities are 200000 then capital is:
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Capital = Assets - Liabilities = 500000 - 200000 = 300000.

text: Assets 800000 and Capital 500000 implies liabilities of:
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Liabilities = Assets - Capital = 800000 - 500000 = 300000.

text: The accounting equation always stays in balance because every transaction has a dual effect.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Each transaction debits and credits equal amounts.

text: Purchasing goods for cash changes which two elements of the accounting equation?
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Stock (an asset) increases and cash (an asset) decreases by the same amount so total assets are unchanged.
explanation: One asset is exchanged for another.

text: A journal entry that involves more than two accounts is called a:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Opening entry|Adjusting entry|Compound entry|Simple entry
explanation: A compound entry records several debits or credits in one entry.

text: The brief explanation written below a journal entry is called the:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Voucher|Narration|Folio|Particulars
explanation: The narration states why the entry was made.

text: Journal entries are recorded in chronological order.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: The journal is a day book so entries follow the date of the transaction.

text: State the double entry rule followed while journalising a transaction.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Debit what comes in or the receiver and credit what goes out or the giver; for every debit there is an equal credit.

text: An increase in a liability account is recorded as a:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Not recorded|Credit|Debit|Either debit or credit
explanation: Liabilities and capital increase on the credit side.

text: Losses and expenses are always:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Capitalised|Debited|Credited|Ignored
explanation: Expenses reduce capital so they are debited.

text: An increase in an asset is recorded on the debit side of its account.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Assets increase by debit and decrease by credit.

text: State the modern rule of debit and credit based on the five groups of accounts.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Debit increases in assets and expenses and decreases in liabilities capital and income; credit the opposite.

text: The process of transferring journal entries to the ledger is called:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Balancing|Casting|Posting|Journalising
explanation: Posting classifies transactions account wise in the ledger.

text: The ledger is also known as the:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Subsidiary book|Memorandum book|Principal book of account|Book of original entry
explanation: All accounts are finally classified in the ledger.

text: Balancing off an account means finding the difference between its debit and credit totals.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: The difference is carried down as the closing balance.

text: What does a debit balance in a personal account indicate?
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: It indicates that the person owes money to the business i.e. a debtor.

text: A trial balance is prepared from the balances of:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Subsidiary books only|Ledger accounts|Journal entries|Cash book only
explanation: It lists every ledger account balance in debit and credit columns.

text: The two sides of a trial balance must always agree in total.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Equal totals are the arithmetical check on posting.

text: Stock in hand appearing in the trial balance is shown only in the:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Balance sheet|Trading account|Profit and loss account|Journal
explanation: Closing stock in the trial balance means it was already adjusted so it appears only as an asset.

text: State the two methods of preparing a trial balance.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: The balance method which lists account balances and the totals method which lists debit and credit totals of each account.

text: Which error IS disclosed by a trial balance?
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Wrong posting to a similar account|Compensating error|Posting only the debit half of an entry|Complete omission of a transaction
explanation: A one sided error disturbs the equality of the two totals.

text: An error of principle such as treating the purchase of machinery as a purchase of goods is disclosed by the trial balance.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Both sides are still equal so the trial balance agrees.

text: Where are petty discrepancies temporarily recorded until the cause is found?
subject: Financial Accounting

text: Distinguish between an error of omission and an error of commission.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: An error of omission is not recording a transaction at all while an error of commission is recording it wrongly in amount account or side.

text: Which expense appears in the trading account?
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Rent of office|Bad debts|Carriage inwards|Office salary
explanation: Carriage inwards is a direct expense on goods purchased.

text: Gross profit is the excess of:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Income over all expenses|Assets over liabilities|Net sales over cost of goods sold|Sales over purchases
explanation: Cost of goods sold is opening stock plus purchases plus direct expenses less closing stock.

text: The trading account shows the operating expenses of the business.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Indirect and operating expenses go to the profit and loss account.

text: State the formula for cost of goods sold.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Opening stock plus purchases plus direct expenses minus closing stock.

text: Net profit is transferred to which account?
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Reserve account|Capital account|Drawings account|Trading account
explanation: Net profit increases the proprietor's capital.

text: Office salaries are classified in the profit and loss account as:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Capital expenditure|Indirect expenses|Direct expenses|Cost of goods sold
explanation: They are administrative expenses not linked to production.

text: The profit and loss account is prepared for a period whereas the balance sheet is prepared as on a date.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: One is a period statement and the other a position statement.

text: State any two items that appear on the credit side of a profit and loss account.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Gross profit brought down and other incomes such as discount received or commission received.

text: Prepaid insurance in a balance sheet is shown as a:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Current asset|Current liability|Fixed asset|Contingent liability
explanation: It is a payment made in advance so it is a short lived asset.

text: Under the order of liquidity the balance sheet lists:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Current assets before fixed assets|Fixed assets before current assets|Liabilities before assets|Capital before assets
explanation: Order of liquidity arranges assets by how quickly they convert to cash.

text: Outstanding wages appear on the liabilities side of the balance sheet.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: They are an amount owed so they are a current liability.

text: Distinguish between a contingent liability and a current liability.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: A contingent liability may or may not arise depending on a future event and is shown as a footnote while a current liability is a definite obligation due within a year.

text: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared by:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: The business entity|The bank|The auditor only|The Reserve Bank
explanation: It is an internal statement reconciling the cash book with the pass book.

text: A cheque issued but not yet presented for payment causes the:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Pass book balance to be higher than the cash book|Cash book balance to be higher than the pass book|Two balances to be equal|Bank to charge interest
explanation: The bank has not yet paid so its recorded balance stays higher.

text: Bank charges appearing in the pass book but not in the cash book are added while preparing the statement starting from the cash book balance.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: They reduce the bank balance so they are deducted.

text: State any two causes of difference between the cash book and the pass book.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Cheques issued but not presented and cheques deposited but not cleared; also bank charges or interest recorded only by the bank.

text: Depreciation on a fixed asset is:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: A gradual loss of value through use and time|A sudden fall in market price|An expense paid in cash each year|A reserve created out of profit
explanation: It allocates the cost of the asset over its useful life.

text: Depreciation on buildings is charged even though their market value may rise.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Depreciation is about using up the asset's service potential not about market prices.

text: Is depreciation a cash expense?
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: No. It is a non cash charge; the cash left the business when the asset was bought.

text: Explain obsolescence as a cause of depreciation.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Obsolescence is the loss of usefulness because a newer technology replaces the asset before its physical life ends.

text: A machine costs 100000 with a scrap value of 10000 and a useful life of 9 years. The annual straight line depreciation is:
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: (Cost - Scrap) / Life = (100000 - 10000) / 9 = 10000 per year.

text: Under the written down value method depreciation is calculated on:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: The book value at the beginning of the year|The original cost every year|The scrap value|The market value
explanation: So the charge falls every year as the balance reduces.

text: The straight line method charges an equal amount of depreciation every year.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: A fixed percentage of the original cost is charged.

text: Which method of depreciation suits an asset whose usage can be measured in output units?
subject: Financial Accounting

text: An invitation to treat is best illustrated by:
subject: Commercial Law
options: An acceptance by phone|Goods displayed in a shop with price tags|A bid at an auction|An offer by letter
explanation: A display invites customers to make an offer; it is not itself an offer.

text: Which is NOT an essential of a valid contract?
subject: Commercial Law
options: Lawful consideration|Free consent|Lawful object|It must be in writing in every case
explanation: An oral contract is valid unless a statute requires writing.

text: An agreement without consideration is generally:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Voidable|Illegal|Void|Valid
explanation: Consideration is essential subject to the exceptions in Section 25.

text: State any four essentials of a valid contract.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: Offer and acceptance; intention to create legal relations; lawful consideration; capacity of parties; free consent; lawful object; certainty and possibility of performance.

text: Consideration must be:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Always equal to the value of the promise|Always in money|Always paid in advance|Real and of some value in the eyes of law
explanation: It need not be adequate but it must be real and lawful.

text: A minor's agreement is:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Void ab initio|Voidable at the minor's option|Valid if the guardian signs|Valid for necessities only
explanation: The Mohori Bibee case settled that a minor cannot contract.

text: Past consideration given at the desire of the promisor is valid consideration in India.
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: Section 2(d) expressly includes past consideration.

text: Who is said to be of sound mind for the purpose of making a contract?
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: A person who at the time of making the contract is capable of understanding it and of forming a rational judgement about its effect on his interests.

text: Consent obtained by threatening to kill a person amounts to:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Undue influence|Misrepresentation|Mistake|Coercion
explanation: Coercion is committing or threatening any act forbidden by the IPC.

text: A false statement of fact made without intent to deceive is:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Undue influence|Misrepresentation|Fraud|Coercion
explanation: Fraud requires the intention to deceive.

text: A contract is discharged by performance when both parties do what they promised.
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: Performance is the most natural mode of discharge.

text: List any four modes by which a contract is discharged.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: By performance; by mutual agreement or novation; by lapse of time; by impossibility or frustration; by breach.

text: A sale and an agreement to sell differ mainly because in a sale:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Only possession passes|The price is always unpaid|The goods must be future goods|Property in the goods passes immediately
explanation: An agreement to sell transfers property at a later date or on a condition.

text: Goods that exist and are owned by the seller at the time of contract are:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Future goods|Contingent goods|Ascertained goods only|Existing goods
explanation: Future goods are yet to be produced or acquired.

text: In a sale the risk of loss passes to the buyer even if the goods are still with the seller.
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: Risk follows ownership unless the parties agree otherwise.

text: Define sale under the Sale of Goods Act 1930.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: A contract where the seller transfers or agrees to transfer the property in goods to the buyer for a price.

text: In a sale on approval the property in the goods passes to the buyer when:
subject: Commercial Law
subtopic: Goods Risk and Transfer of Property
options: The goods are delivered for trial|The price is fixed|The seller issues an invoice|The buyer signifies approval or keeps the goods beyond the trial period
explanation: Until then the goods remain the seller's and can be returned.

text: Under the Sale of Goods Act the term goods includes:
subject: Commercial Law
subtopic: Goods Risk and Transfer of Property
options: Only movable articles|Money that is legal tender|Immovable property|Stocks and shares and growing crops
explanation: Goods means every kind of movable property other than actionable claims and money.

text: Unascertained goods can be the subject of an immediate sale.
subject: Commercial Law
subtopic: Goods Risk and Transfer of Property
explanation: Property cannot pass until the goods are ascertained.

text: What is meant by transfer of property in goods?
subject: Commercial Law
subtopic: Goods Risk and Transfer of Property
correctAnswer: It means the passing of ownership from the seller to the buyer.

text: A stipulation essential to the main purpose of the contract is a:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Condition|Warranty|Representation|Caveat
explanation: Breach of a condition gives the right to repudiate the contract.

text: A breach of warranty gives the buyer the right to:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Claim damages only|Reject the goods|Treat the contract as void|Refuse to pay the price
explanation: A warranty is collateral so the contract survives.

text: Caveat emptor means let the buyer beware.
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: It is the general rule subject to the implied conditions.

text: State the implied condition as to merchantable quality.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: Goods sold by description must be of merchantable quality i.e. fit for the purpose for which such goods are usually bought.

text: How many parties are there in a promissory note?
subject: Commercial Law
options: Three — drawer drawee and payee|One only|Four|Two — maker and payee
explanation: The maker promises to pay the payee.

text: A promissory note must be:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Oral and witnessed|Registered|Stamped by a notary|In writing and signed by the maker
explanation: An oral promise to pay is not a negotiable instrument.

text: A promissory note requires acceptance by the payee before it becomes valid.
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: Only a bill of exchange requires acceptance.

text: Can a promissory note be made payable to the maker himself?
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: No. The maker and the payee cannot be the same person.

text: A bill of exchange involves how many parties?
subject: Commercial Law
options: One|Three — drawer drawee and payee|Two|Four
explanation: The drawer orders the drawee to pay the payee.

text: A cheque is always drawn on:
subject: Commercial Law
options: A specified banker|Any person|The Reserve Bank only|A notary public
explanation: Section 6 defines a cheque as a bill drawn on a specified banker payable on demand.

text: A cheque is payable on demand and requires no acceptance.
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: Unlike a bill it is never presented for acceptance.

text: What is meant by dishonour of a cheque?
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: The bank's refusal to pay the cheque usually for insufficient funds; the drawer can be liable under Section 138.

text: A holder in due course must take the instrument:
subject: Commercial Law
options: For consideration before maturity and in good faith|After maturity|Without consideration|Only by inheritance
explanation: Those three conditions give the holder a better title than the transferor.

text: A holder in due course takes the instrument free from defects in the title of the transferor.
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: That is the main privilege of being a holder in due course.

text: Crossing a cheque means:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Cancelling the cheque|Signing it twice|Endorsing it to a third party|Drawing two parallel lines on its face so it is paid only through a bank
explanation: Crossing makes payment safer by routing it through a bank account.

text: Distinguish between a holder and a holder in due course.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: A holder is anyone entitled to possess the instrument and recover the amount due; a holder in due course is a holder who took it for consideration before maturity in good faith and without notice of any defect.

text: Which Act did the Consumer Protection Act 2019 replace?
subject: Commercial Law
options: The Indian Contract Act 1872|The Sale of Goods Act 1930|The Companies Act 2013|The Consumer Protection Act 1986
explanation: The 2019 Act widened the definition of consumer and added e-commerce.

text: Under the 2019 Act a person who buys goods for resale is:
subject: Commercial Law
options: A consumer|A complainant|A beneficiary|Not a consumer
explanation: Commercial purpose excludes a buyer from the definition.

text: The Central Consumer Protection Authority was created by the 2019 Act.
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: It regulates matters relating to unfair trade practices and false advertising.

text: State any two changes brought in by the Consumer Protection Act 2019.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: Creation of the CCPA; inclusion of e-commerce and telemarketing; wider pecuniary jurisdiction; mediation cells; product liability.

text: How many basic consumer rights are recognised in India?
subject: Commercial Law
options: Six|Four|Eight|Ten
explanation: Safety information choice representation redressal and consumer education.

text: The right to be protected against marketing of hazardous goods is the right to:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Safety|Choice|Redressal|Information
explanation: It is the first of the six rights.

text: The right to consumer education is one of the recognised consumer rights.
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: It ensures consumers acquire the knowledge to make informed choices.

text: List the six rights of a consumer.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: Right to safety; right to be informed; right to choose; right to be heard or represented; right to seek redressal; right to consumer education.

text: The three tier consumer redressal machinery consists of:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Lok Adalat and Arbitration only|Police Courts and Magistrates|District State and National Commissions|Civil High and Supreme Courts only
explanation: Each tier has its own pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction.

text: Deficiency in service means:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Only a delay in service|A rude employee|Overcharging alone|Any fault imperfection or inadequacy in the quality or standard of service
explanation: The definition covers quality nature and manner of performance.

text: A consumer complaint can be filed only by the consumer who bought the goods personally.
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: A recognised voluntary organisation or the government may also complain.

text: What is an unfair trade practice?
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: A trade practice that misrepresents the price quality or utility of goods or services to promote sale and causes loss or injury to a consumer.

text: The probability of a sure event is:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: 0|0.5|Infinity|1
explanation: Probability ranges from 0 for impossible to 1 for certain.

text: Two events that cannot occur together are called:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Independent|Exhaustive|Equally likely|Mutually exclusive
explanation: For them P(A and B) = 0.

text: A single die is thrown. The probability of NOT getting a 6 is:
subject: Business Mathematics

text: State the classical definition of probability.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: The ratio of the number of favourable equally likely outcomes to the total number of possible outcomes.

text: The conditional probability of A given B equals:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: P(B) divided by P(A)|P(A and B) divided by P(B)|P(A) multiplied by P(B)|P(A) plus P(B)
explanation: It is the probability of A given that B has occurred.

text: Bayes theorem is used to compute:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: A correlation coefficient|A posterior probability from prior probabilities|The mean of grouped data|The variance of a sample
explanation: It revises a prior belief using new evidence.

text: For two dependent events the joint probability equals the probability of the first event multiplied by the conditional probability of the second given the first.
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: That is the multiplication rule for dependent events.

text: State Bayes theorem in words.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: The probability of a cause given an observed effect equals the prior probability of that cause times the probability of the effect given the cause divided by the total probability of the effect.

text: The standard deviation is:
subject: Business Mathematics
subtopic: Measures of Dispersion and Central Tendency
options: The square of the variance|The mean of the deviations|The largest deviation|The positive square root of the variance
explanation: It restores the unit of the original data.

text: Which measure of central tendency is not affected by extreme values?
subject: Business Mathematics
subtopic: Measures of Dispersion and Central Tendency
options: Weighted mean|Median|Arithmetic mean|Harmonic mean
explanation: The median depends on position not magnitude.

text: The coefficient of variation is expressed as a percentage.
subject: Business Mathematics
subtopic: Measures of Dispersion and Central Tendency
explanation: It is the standard deviation divided by the mean times 100.

text: Why is the standard deviation considered the best measure of dispersion?
subject: Business Mathematics
subtopic: Measures of Dispersion and Central Tendency
correctAnswer: It uses every observation is rigidly defined is capable of further algebraic treatment and is less affected by sampling fluctuations.

text: In an index number the period against which comparisons are made is the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Base year|Current year|Average year|Reporting year
explanation: The base year value is taken as 100.

text: The simple aggregate price index is the ratio of:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: The sum of current year prices to the sum of base year prices times 100|The sum of quantities to the sum of prices|The geometric mean of relatives|The average of price relatives divided by 100
explanation: It is also called the aggregate index method.

text: Weights are used in a weighted index number.
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: Weights are usually the base year quantities or values.

text: State any two characteristics of an index number.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: It is a relative expressed in percentage form; it measures average change over time or space; it is based on a base period taken as 100.

text: Laspeyres price index uses quantities of the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Current year as weights|Average of both years|Value of imports|Base year as weights
explanation: Paasche uses current year quantities.

text: Fishers ideal index is the geometric mean of the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Price and quantity indices|Base and current indices|Laspeyres and Paasche indices|Simple and weighted indices
explanation: It satisfies both the time reversal and factor reversal tests.

text: Fishers ideal index satisfies the time reversal test.
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: Working forwards and backwards gives a consistent result.

text: Why is Fishers index called ideal?
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: Because it is based on both years' quantities and it alone satisfies the time reversal and factor reversal tests.

text: The consumer price index is used mainly to measure:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Government revenue|The change in the cost of living of a group of consumers|Industrial output|Company profits
explanation: It tracks the prices of a fixed basket of goods and services households buy.

text: Dearness allowance to employees is usually revised on the basis of the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Index of industrial production|Sensex|Consumer price index|Wholesale price index
explanation: It offsets inflation in the cost of living.

text: A consumer price index is mainly useful for measuring household inflation.
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: That is its principal use.

text: State any four uses of index numbers.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: Measuring inflation; revising wages and dearness allowance; guiding government policy; deflating nominal values to real values; comparing performance across periods or regions.

text: Which is NOT a component of a time series?
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Cross sectional variation|Trend|Seasonal variation|Cyclical variation
explanation: The four components are trend seasonal cyclical and irregular.

text: The component that shows a long term direction in the data is the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Cyclical variation|Trend|Seasonal variation|Irregular variation
explanation: It reflects sustained growth or decline.

text: The irregular component of a time series can be predicted accurately.
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: It arises from unforeseen events such as floods or strikes.

text: Define a time series.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: A set of observations of a variable arranged in chronological order at equal time intervals.

text: The moving average method is used to measure the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Cyclical amplitude|Trend|Seasonal index|Irregular component
explanation: It smooths short term fluctuations to reveal the trend.

text: Seasonal variation is measured over a period of:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Five years|A business cycle|One year or less|Ten years
explanation: It repeats regularly within a year.

text: An even period moving average requires centring of the values.
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: The average falls between two periods so it is centred by a second two period average.

text: State the two commonly used methods of measuring trend.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: The graphic or freehand curve method and the method of least squares fitting a trend line.

text: The business cycle consists of:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Inflation and deflation|Prosperity recession depression and recovery|Only boom and bust|Trend and seasonality
explanation: These four phases repeat over several years.

text: Cyclical variations are periodic and their period is fixed in advance.
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: Each cycle differs in length and amplitude so they are not strictly periodic.

text: The business cycle is best described as:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: A sudden jump caused by a disaster|A permanent shift in the level|Fluctuations about the trend over more than a year|A change within one year
explanation: It is a wave like movement around the long term trend.

text: Explain the concept of the business cycle.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: It is the recurring rise and fall in economic activity over more than a year passing through prosperity recession depression and recovery phases.

text: In a linear programming problem the objective function must be:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Constant|Non linear but differentiable|Linear in the decision variables|Quadratic
explanation: Linearity of both objective and constraints is what makes it an LPP.

text: The unknown quantities to be determined in an LPP are the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Decision variables|Slack variables|Objective coefficients|Constraints
explanation: They are the quantities the manager controls.

text: The non negativity restriction means the decision variables cannot be negative.
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: Quantities produced or purchased cannot be less than zero.

text: State the three components of a linear programming problem.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: An objective function to be maximised or minimised; a set of linear constraints; and non negativity restrictions on the decision variables.

text: The feasible region of an LPP is:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: The set of corner points only|The set of points satisfying all constraints simultaneously|The set of optimal points|The area above the objective line
explanation: It is the common region of all the constraints including non negativity.

text: In the graphical method the optimal value occurs at:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Any interior point|A corner point of the feasible region|The centre of the region|The origin always
explanation: That is the corner point theorem.

text: The feasible region of a linear programming problem is always a convex set.
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: It is bounded by straight lines so any line segment between two feasible points is feasible.

text: State the steps of the graphical method for a two variable LPP.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: Convert each inequality to an equation and plot the lines; identify the half plane satisfying each; find the common feasible region; evaluate the objective function at every corner point; choose the maximum or minimum.

text: Slack variables are added to convert:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: The objective function into a constraint|Negative variables into positive ones|Less than or equal to constraints into equations|Greater than or equal to constraints into equations
explanation: They measure unused capacity of a resource.

text: The coefficient of a slack variable in the objective function is:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: One|The same as the decision variable|Negative one|Zero
explanation: Unused capacity contributes nothing to profit.

text: The simplex method moves from one basic feasible solution to a better one until optimality is reached.
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: Each iteration improves the objective value.

text: What is a basic feasible solution?
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: A solution obtained by setting the non basic variables to zero that satisfies all constraints and the non negativity conditions.

text: The law of demand states that other things remaining the same:
subject: Economics
options: Quantity demanded rises when price falls|Quantity demanded rises when price rises|Demand equals supply at every price|Price is determined by income
explanation: There is an inverse relation between price and quantity demanded.

text: The demand curve normally slopes:
subject: Economics
options: Downward from left to right|Upward from left to right|Vertically|Horizontally
explanation: Reflecting the inverse price quantity relation.

text: Which is an exception to the law of demand?
subject: Economics
options: Giffen goods|Normal goods|Substitute goods|Complementary goods
explanation: For a Giffen good demand rises as price rises.

text: State any two assumptions of the law of demand.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: No change in consumer income; no change in the prices of related goods; no change in tastes; no expectation of future price change.

text: Price elasticity of demand is measured as:
subject: Economics
options: Quantity demanded divided by price|The slope of the supply curve|Percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price|Change in price divided by change in quantity
explanation: It measures responsiveness of demand to a price change.

text: Demand for a necessity tends to be:
subject: Economics
options: Perfectly elastic|Unitary|Inelastic|Elastic
explanation: Consumers keep buying it even when the price rises.

text: A perfectly inelastic demand curve is a vertical straight line.
subject: Economics
explanation: Quantity does not respond at all to price.

text: Perfectly elastic demand has a price elasticity of:
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Infinity. A horizontal demand curve where any price rise reduces quantity demanded to zero.

text: Market equilibrium occurs where:
subject: Economics
options: Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied|Price is lowest|Supply is greatest|Total revenue is maximum
explanation: There is no tendency for the price to change at that point.

text: An increase in supply with unchanged demand causes the equilibrium price to:
subject: Economics
options: Stay the same|Become indeterminate|Fall|Rise
explanation: A surplus at the old price pushes it down.

text: A shift of the demand curve is caused by a change in:
subject: Economics
options: The price of the good itself|The quantity supplied|The cost of production|Consumer income
explanation: A change in the good's own price causes a movement along the curve not a shift.

text: Distinguish between a movement along the demand curve and a shift of the demand curve.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: A movement along is caused by a change in the price of the good itself and changes quantity demanded; a shift is caused by a change in a determinant such as income or tastes and changes demand at every price.

text: The income method computes national income by adding:
subject: Economics
options: Exports minus imports|Compensation of employees operating surplus and net factor income from abroad|Consumption investment and government spending|Value added by all firms
explanation: It sums the factor incomes generated in production.

text: The expenditure method expresses national income as:
subject: Economics
options: W plus R plus I plus P|Output minus intermediate consumption|GDP minus depreciation|C plus I plus G plus net exports
explanation: It sums final expenditure on goods and services.

text: The value added method avoids the problem of:
subject: Economics
options: Black money|Non monetised output|Double counting|Transfer payments
explanation: Only the value added at each stage is counted.

text: List any three problems in the measurement of national income.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Double counting; non monetised subsistence output; black money; lack of reliable data; transfer payments being wrongly included.

text: GNP at market prices equals GDP at market prices plus:
subject: Economics
subtopic: GDP GNP and Per Capita Income
options: Subsidies|Net factor income from abroad|Net indirect taxes|Depreciation
explanation: GNP counts income earned by nationals wherever located.

text: GDP at factor cost is obtained from GDP at market prices by:
subject: Economics
subtopic: GDP GNP and Per Capita Income
options: Adding depreciation|Subtracting net factor income from abroad|Subtracting net indirect taxes|Adding net indirect taxes
explanation: Net indirect taxes are indirect taxes less subsidies.

text: Per capita income is national income divided by population.
subject: Economics
subtopic: GDP GNP and Per Capita Income
explanation: It is the average income per person.

text: Distinguish between GDP and GNP.
subject: Economics
subtopic: GDP GNP and Per Capita Income
correctAnswer: GDP measures the value of final goods produced within the domestic territory while GNP adds net factor income from abroad so it measures income of the nationals.

text: Which of the following is EXCLUDED from national income?
subject: Economics
options: Old age pension|Salary of a teacher|Rent of a house|Interest on a loan
explanation: A pension is a transfer payment with no current production behind it.

text: The problem of double counting is avoided by:
subject: Economics
options: Using only the income method|Counting only value added at each stage|Counting every transaction twice|Ignoring intermediate goods prices
explanation: Alternatively only final goods are counted.

text: Unpaid household work is included in the national income of India.
subject: Economics
explanation: It is a non monetised service and is left out.

text: Explain why non monetised sectors create a problem in measuring national income.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: In subsistence farming and household production goods and services are not sold so no market price exists and their contribution is under recorded.

text: Which is the primary function of money?
subject: Economics
options: Store of value|Standard of deferred payment|Unit of account|Medium of exchange
explanation: It removes the need for a double coincidence of wants.

text: Fiat money is money that:
subject: Economics
options: Has value only by government decree|Is made of gold|Can be exchanged for bullion|Is used only in barter
explanation: Its face value far exceeds its material value.

text: Money acting as a store of value allows purchasing power to be saved for the future.
subject: Economics
explanation: That is one of its secondary functions.

text: State the four functions of money.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Medium of exchange; measure of value or unit of account; store of value; standard of deferred payments.

text: The central bank of India is:
subject: Economics
options: NABARD|The Ministry of Finance|The Reserve Bank of India|The State Bank of India
explanation: It was established in 1935 and nationalised in 1949.

text: The monopoly of issuing currency notes in India rests with:
subject: Economics
options: The Reserve Bank of India|Commercial banks|The Central Government directly|The Securities and Exchange Board
explanation: One rupee notes and coins are issued by the Government.

text: The Reserve Bank of India accepts deposits from the general public.
subject: Economics
explanation: It deals with banks and the government not with the public.

text: State any three functions of a central bank.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Issue of currency; banker to the government; banker's bank and supervisor; custodian of foreign exchange reserves; controller of credit.

text: The cash reserve ratio is the portion of deposits that banks must keep with:
subject: Economics
options: The Central Government|Other commercial banks|The Reserve Bank of India as cash|Their own vaults only
explanation: It earns no interest and is a tool of credit control.

text: An increase in the repo rate usually:
subject: Economics
options: Makes borrowing costlier for banks and contracts credit|Expands credit|Has no effect on lending|Reduces the cash reserve ratio
explanation: It is a contractionary monetary policy measure.

text: Credit creation by commercial banks is limited by the cash reserve ratio.
subject: Economics
explanation: A higher reserve ratio lowers the credit multiplier.

text: Explain the credit creation function of commercial banks.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Banks lend out a part of their deposits keeping only the required reserve; the loan is credited to a deposit account which is spent and returns to the banking system as fresh deposits; the process repeats so total deposits become a multiple of the initial deposit.

text: A country has a comparative advantage in producing a good when its:
subject: Economics
options: Output is largest|Wage rate is highest|Opportunity cost of producing that good is lower|Absolute cost is lowest
explanation: David Ricardo's theory explains trade even without absolute advantage.

text: The Heckscher Ohlin theory explains trade on the basis of:
subject: Economics
options: Technology alone|Transport costs|Government policy|Factor endowments
explanation: A country exports goods that use its abundant factor intensively.

text: Free trade allows each country to specialise according to comparative advantage.
subject: Economics
explanation: Specialisation raises total world output.

text: Distinguish between free trade and protectionism.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Free trade allows goods to move across borders without restrictions while protectionism uses tariffs quotas and subsidies to restrict imports and shield domestic producers.

text: The balance of payments records:
subject: Economics
subtopic: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates
options: Only capital flows|All economic transactions between residents and the rest of the world|Only visible trade|Only government transactions
explanation: It has a current account and a capital account.

text: The current account of the balance of payments records:
subject: Economics
subtopic: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates
options: Changes in foreign exchange reserves|Trade in goods and services plus income and transfers|Foreign direct investment|Loans from abroad
explanation: Investment and loans belong to the capital account.

text: A depreciation of the rupee makes Indian exports cheaper for foreign buyers.
subject: Economics
subtopic: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates
explanation: It tends to encourage exports and discourage imports.

text: When is the balance of payments said to be in equilibrium?
subject: Economics
subtopic: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates
correctAnswer: When autonomous receipts from the rest of the world equal autonomous payments so no change in official reserves is needed.

text: A tax levied on imported goods is called:
subject: Economics
options: A subsidy|A tariff|A quota|An excise duty
explanation: It raises the price of imports to protect domestic producers.

text: The World Trade Organization was established in:
subject: Economics
explanation: It replaced GATT and is based in Geneva.

text: A quota is a quantitative limit on the amount of a good that may be imported.
subject: Economics
explanation: It restricts quantity rather than price.

text: State any two functions of the World Trade Organization.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Administering trade agreements; providing a forum for trade negotiations; settling trade disputes; reviewing national trade policies.

text: The words socialist and secular were inserted into the Preamble by the:
subject: Political Science
options: 44th Amendment|1st Amendment|86th Amendment|42nd Amendment
explanation: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 adopted the famous Kiriti mantra language.

text: Articles 12 to 35 of the Constitution deal with:
subject: Political Science
options: Fundamental Duties|Directive Principles of State Policy|Emergency powers|Fundamental Rights
explanation: Part III of the Constitution contains the fundamental rights.

text: List any four fundamental freedoms guaranteed by Article 19.
subject: Political Science
correctAnswer: Freedom of speech and expression; to assemble peacefully; to form associations; to move freely; to reside and settle anywhere; and to practice any profession.

text: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha under the Constitution is:
subject: Political Science
explanation: Article 81 fixes the ceiling at 552 members (530 elected and 20 nominated).

text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha. This statement is:
subject: Political Science
explanation: The members of the house elect their own Speaker by majority vote.

text: State any three powers of the Rajya Sabha in relation to money bills.
subject: Political Science
correctAnswer: It may recommend changes to a money bill; it can hold the bill for at most six days; and it cannot reject the bill.

text: The basic structure doctrine was upheld in the:
subject: Political Science
options: Shankari Prasad case|Golaknath case|Menaka case|Kesavananda Bharati case
explanation: The 1973 judgment held that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.

text: The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court extends to disputes between the Government of India and a state or between states. This statement is:
subject: Political Science
explanation: Such disputes are directly heard by the Supreme Court under Article 131.

text: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment of 1992 gave constitutional status to:
subject: Political Science
options: Cooperative societies|Municipal corporations|Urban local bodies|Panchayats
explanation: It added the eleventh schedule covering panchayat functions.

text: The 74th Constitutional Amendment deals with:
subject: Political Science
subtopic: Urban Local Bodies and the 74th Amendment
options: Municipal and urban local bodies|Village panchayats|The higher judiciary|Centre state finance
explanation: It came into force in 1993 and strengthened urban local government.

text: The Gram Sabha consists of all persons registered in the electoral roll of the village. This statement is:
subject: Political Science
explanation: It is the basic unit of direct self governance at the village level.

text: The District Planning Committee prepares the plan for the district as a whole. This statement is:
subject: Political Science
explanation: It consolidates the plans of the panchayats and municipal bodies into a district plan.

text: The Rig Veda is the:
subject: History
options: Book of law|Collection of dramas|Oldest Veda; a collection of hymns to gods|Latest of the four Vedas
explanation: It contains 1028 hymns in ten mandalas and is the earliest Vedic text.

text: The Vedic society saw the gradual development of the varna based social structure. This statement is:
subject: History
explanation: The later Vedic texts describe the four varnas of brahmana; kshatriya; vaishya; and shudra.

text: Akbar's Din-i Ilahi was a syncretic faith he promoted to unite different religious groups. This statement is:
subject: History
explanation: It blended elements of Hinduism and Islam and was close to a court philosophy rather than a mass religion.

text: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 with A. O. Hume as its key founder. This statement is:
subject: History
subtopic: Rise of the Indian National Congress
explanation: The first session at Bombay in 1885 was presided by W. C. Bonnerjee.

text: The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 symbolized the beginning of the end of the Cold War era. This statement is:
subject: History
subtopic: World Wars and the United Nations
explanation: German reunification followed in 1990 and the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991.

text: Socialization is the process by which a person learns and internalizes the norms of society. This statement is:
subject: Sociology
explanation: It begins in the family and continues through school; peers; and media.

text: The primary agent of socialization is the:
subject: Sociology
options: Army|Market|State|Family
explanation: The family is where children first learn language; norms; and roles.

text: The family is called a primary group because its members have direct and intimate face to face interaction. This statement is:
subject: Sociology
explanation: Cooley used the term primary group for small groups with warm personal contact.

text: Marriage systems studied in sociology include:
subject: Sociology
options: Monogamy only|Polyandry only|None of these|Monogamy and polygamy
explanation: Polygamy further includes polygyny (one husband many wives) and polyandry (one wife many husbands).

text: Education as a social institution functions to transmit knowledge and socialize the young. This statement is:
subject: Sociology
explanation: It also sorts people into roles through credentials and skills.

text: Social mobility refers to the movement of people between social strata. This statement is:
subject: Sociology
explanation: It can be vertical (up or down) or horizontal (across groups at the same level).

text: The jajmani system refers to hereditary patron client relations between caste groups. This statement is:
subject: Sociology
explanation: Artisans received a share of produce and services in return for their work.

text: A social movement is organized collective effort to promote or resist social change. This statement is:
subject: Sociology
explanation: Examples are the independence movement; the women's movement; and environmental movements.

text: Globalization affects society mainly through faster flows of goods; capital; people; and ideas. This statement is:
subject: Sociology
explanation: It also reshapes local cultures and labour markets.

text: State any three factors of social change in India.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: Education; industrialization; urbanization; legal reforms such as personal law changes; and globalization.

text: The structuralist school that analyzed conscious experience was founded by:
subject: Psychology
options: Ivan Pavlov|B. F. Skinner|William James|Wilhelm Wundt
explanation: Wundt set up the first psychology laboratory at Leipzig in 1879.

text: The functionalist school emphasized the functions of behaviour and consciousness. This statement is:
subject: Psychology
explanation: Led by William James it asked what mental processes do for the organism.

text: The idea of tabula rasa (mind as a blank slate) is associated with:
subject: Psychology
options: John Locke|Sigmund Freud|Abraham Maslow|Jean Piaget
explanation: Locke argued that experience writes all knowledge onto the empty mind of the child.

text: State three major approaches in modern psychology.
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: Behaviourism; cognitivism; and psychoanalysis; with the biological and humanistic approaches adding further perspectives.

text: Classical conditioning is associated with:
subject: Psychology
options: Edward Thorndike|Albert Bandura|B. F. Skinner|Ivan Pavlov
explanation: Pavlov's dogs learned to salivate to a bell that predicted food.

text: Operant conditioning modifies behaviour through:
subject: Psychology
options: Dream analysis|Reinforcement and punishment|Stimulus pairing only|Observation only
explanation: Consequences determine how likely a voluntary behaviour is to repeat.

text: The law of effect states that behaviour followed by a satisfying consequence is more likely to recur. This statement is:
subject: Psychology
explanation: Thorndike proposed it from his puzzle box experiments with cats.

text: Short term memory can hold roughly seven plus or minus two items. This statement is:
subject: Psychology
explanation: Miller's finding describes the limited capacity of working memory without rehearsal.

text: Distinguish between classical and operant conditioning.
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: Classical conditioning pairs stimuli to produce an involuntary response; operant conditioning shapes voluntary behaviour using its consequences such as reinforcement and punishment.

text: The intelligence quotient is computed as mental age divided by chronological age multiplied by 100. This statement is:
subject: Psychology
explanation: This ratio formula was used in early intelligence testing before deviation based scores.

text: Alfred Binet is credited with developing the first practical:
subject: Psychology
options: Psychotherapy technique|Reflex test|Personality scale|IQ test for children
explanation: He and Simon designed school tests to identify pupils needing help.

text: Howard Gardner proposed the theory of:
subject: Psychology
options: Only spatial intelligence|A single general intelligence|Multiple intelligences|No measurable intelligence
explanation: He listed linguistic; logical mathematical; musical; bodily kinesthetic; and other distinct intelligences.

text: The g factor in intelligence theory refers to a general mental ability common to all cognitive tasks. This statement is:
subject: Psychology
explanation: Spearman identified it from the positive correlations among test scores.

text: List the three components of Sternberg's triarchic theory of intelligence.
subject: Psychology

text: A mental disorder can be defined as a syndrome of clinically significant disturbance in cognition; emotion; or behaviour. This statement is:
subject: Psychology
explanation: The definition stresses distress or impairment in addition to the symptoms.

text: A common symptom of anxiety disorders is:
subject: Psychology
options: Headache only|Excessive worry and tension|High blood pressure only|Fever only
explanation: Worry; restlessness; and muscle tension are core features.

text: Cognitive behavioural therapy works by changing maladaptive thoughts and behaviours. This statement is:
subject: Psychology
explanation: It is a structured short term approach with strong evidence for depression and anxiety.

text: Stress is the body's response to any demand that upsets its balance. This statement is:
subject: Psychology
explanation: The demand is called a stressor and the response mobilizes the body to cope.

text: List three signs that a person may need professional mental health support.
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: Persistent sadness or loss of interest; major changes in sleep or appetite; and social withdrawal or impaired daily functioning.

text: The Preamble declares India to be a:
subject: Political Science
options: Unitary constitutional monarchy|Confederation of states|Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic|Federal theocratic state
explanation: Those are the adjectives the Preamble uses for the Indian Union.

text: The idea of beginning a constitution with a preamble was borrowed from:
subject: Political Science
options: The Constitution of the United States of America|The Constitution of the United Kingdom|The Constitution of Ireland|The Constitution of Canada
explanation: The American Constitution was the first to begin with a preamble.

text: The words socialist secular and integrity were added to the Preamble by the:
subject: Political Science
options: 44th Amendment Act 1978|1st Amendment Act 1951|73rd Amendment Act 1992|42nd Amendment Act 1976
explanation: It is the only amendment that has changed the Preamble so far.

text: The Preamble is a part of the Constitution of India.
subject: Political Science
explanation: The Supreme Court held so in the LIC of India case.

text: The right to equality before law is guaranteed by Article:
subject: Political Science
explanation: Article 14 forbids discrimination and guarantees equal protection of the laws.

text: Untouchability was abolished by Article:
subject: Political Science
explanation: Its practice in any form is forbidden and punishable by law.

text: Article 19 guarantees how many freedoms?
subject: Political Science
options: Seven|Five|Four|Six
explanation: Speech and expression assembly association movement residence and profession.

text: Fundamental rights in India are absolute and can never be restricted.
subject: Political Science
explanation: They are subject to reasonable restrictions on grounds such as sovereignty public order and morality.

text: Under which Article can the Supreme Court issue writs to enforce fundamental rights?
subject: Political Science
options: Article 14|Article 143|Article 32|Article 226
explanation: Ambedkar called Article 32 the heart and soul of the Constitution.

text: The writ that requires a detained person to be produced before the court is:
subject: Political Science
options: Mandamus|Certiorari|Quo warranto|Habeas corpus
explanation: It literally means to have the body.

text: Mandamus is issued to:
subject: Political Science
options: Transfer a case to a higher court|Question the title to a public office|Release a detained person|Command a public authority to perform its duty
explanation: It lies against a public body that has failed to act.

text: Fundamental rights can be suspended during a national emergency.
subject: Political Science
explanation: Under Article 359 although Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended.

text: The Parliament of India consists of:
subject: Political Science
options: The President the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha|Only the two Houses|The Lok Sabha and the Council of Ministers|The Prime Minister and both Houses
explanation: The President is an integral part of Parliament.

text: Which House of Parliament is never dissolved?
subject: Political Science
options: Both are dissolved|The Legislative Council|Rajya Sabha|Lok Sabha
explanation: It is a permanent body with one third of its members retiring every two years.

text: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is:
subject: Political Science
explanation: Of these 238 represent the states and union territories and 12 are nominated by the President.

text: The term of a member of the Rajya Sabha is six years.
subject: Political Science
explanation: Except for a member elected to fill a casual vacancy.

text: A money bill can be introduced only in the:
subject: Political Science
options: Either House without permission|State Legislative Assembly only|Lok Sabha with the prior recommendation of the President|Rajya Sabha
explanation: Article 110 defines what a money bill is.

text: The Rajya Sabha must return a money bill to the Lok Sabha within:
subject: Political Science
options: 30 days|7 days|60 days|14 days
explanation: It may recommend amendments but the Lok Sabha is free to reject them.

text: Who decides whether a bill is a money bill?
subject: Political Science
options: The Prime Minister|The Speaker of the Lok Sabha|The President|The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
explanation: The Speaker's certificate on the question is final.

text: A money bill can be introduced first in the Rajya Sabha.
subject: Political Science
explanation: Only the Lok Sabha can originate a money bill.

text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by:
subject: Political Science
options: The members of the Lok Sabha|The President|The members of both Houses|The Council of Ministers
explanation: The election is held as soon as possible after a general election.

text: The ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is:
subject: Political Science
options: The President|The Prime Minister|The senior most member|The Vice President of India
explanation: The Deputy Chairman is elected from among its own members.

text: A joint sitting of the two Houses is presided over by the:
subject: Political Science
options: Speaker of the Lok Sabha|Chairman of the Rajya Sabha|President|Chief Justice of India
explanation: The President summons the joint sitting but does not preside over it.

text: State any three powers of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
subject: Political Science
correctAnswer: Maintains order in the House; decides whether a bill is a money bill; presides over a joint sitting; interprets the rules of procedure; puts the question and announces the result of voting.

text: The Supreme Court of India is located in:
subject: Political Science
options: Kolkata|Chennai|New Delhi|Mumbai
explanation: It first sat on 28 January 1950.

text: A judge of the Supreme Court holds office until the age of:
