subject: Political Science
options: 70 years|65 years|62 years|60 years
explanation: Judges of the High Courts retire at 62.

text: Disputes between the Government of India and one or more States fall under which jurisdiction?
subject: Political Science
options: Appellate jurisdiction|Advisory jurisdiction|Writ jurisdiction|Original jurisdiction
explanation: Article 131 provides for this original jurisdiction.

text: The President may seek the opinion of the Supreme Court under Article:
subject: Political Science
explanation: That is the advisory jurisdiction of the Court.

text: The basic structure doctrine was propounded in the:
subject: Political Science
options: Maneka Gandhi case of 1978|Kesavananda Bharati case of 1973|Golak Nath case of 1967|Minerva Mills case of 1980
explanation: It held that Parliament cannot alter the basic features of the Constitution.

text: Judicial review is the power of the courts to:
subject: Political Science
options: Frame the budget|Examine the constitutionality of legislative and executive acts|Make laws for the country|Appoint ministers
explanation: It keeps the other organs of government within the Constitution.

text: Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution including its basic features.
subject: Political Science
explanation: The basic structure lies beyond the amending power.

text: What is meant by judicial review?
subject: Political Science
correctAnswer: The power of the judiciary to examine whether laws and executive actions conform to the Constitution and to declare them void if they do not.

text: Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the:
subject: Political Science
options: Prime Minister|Chief Minister|Parliament by vote|President of India
explanation: In practice the President acts on the recommendation of the collegium.

text: The collegium system for appointing judges consists of:
subject: Political Science
options: The President and the Prime Minister|The Law Minister and the Attorney General|A standing committee of Parliament|The Chief Justice of India and the senior most judges of the Supreme Court
explanation: It evolved through the Second and Third Judges cases.

text: The salaries of Supreme Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
subject: Political Science
explanation: That places them beyond the annual vote of Parliament and protects independence.

text: Explain the collegium system for judicial appointments.
subject: Political Science
correctAnswer: A body headed by the Chief Justice of India with the four senior most judges recommends appointments and transfers to the President; the government may return a name once but must accept a recommendation that the collegium reiterates.

text: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 gave constitutional status to:
subject: Political Science
options: District collectors|Panchayati Raj institutions|Urban local bodies|The Election Commission
explanation: It added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.

text: Which Schedule lists the matters that may be entrusted to a Panchayat?
subject: Political Science
options: Ninth Schedule|Eleventh Schedule|Twelfth Schedule|Tenth Schedule
explanation: It contains 29 functional items.

text: The three tier Panchayati Raj structure operates at the:
subject: Political Science
options: Ward and city levels|Block and tehsil levels only|Village intermediate and district levels|State and national levels only
explanation: Gram Panchayat Panchayat Samiti and Zilla Parishad.

text: The 73rd Amendment reserves seats for women in Panchayats.
subject: Political Science
explanation: Not less than one third of seats and of chairperson posts are reserved for women.

text: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act deals with:
subject: Political Science
subtopic: Urban Local Bodies and the 74th Amendment
options: The Election Commission|Municipalities and other urban local bodies|Panchayats|Union Territories
explanation: It added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule.

text: Which is NOT an urban local body created by the 74th Amendment?
subject: Political Science
subtopic: Urban Local Bodies and the 74th Amendment
options: Nagar Panchayat|Municipal Council|Municipal Corporation|Zilla Parishad
explanation: Zilla Parishad is the rural district tier under the 73rd Amendment.

text: A Nagar Panchayat is constituted for:
subject: Political Science
subtopic: Urban Local Bodies and the 74th Amendment
options: A transitional area between rural and urban|A metropolitan city|A cantonment|A state capital
explanation: The Governor notifies such transitional areas.

text: Urban local bodies derive their powers from the State Legislature.
subject: Political Science
subtopic: Urban Local Bodies and the 74th Amendment
explanation: Local government and public health are entries in the State List.

text: The Gram Sabha consists of:
subject: Political Science
options: Village elders nominated by the Sarpanch|All persons registered in the electoral roll of the village area|Only the elected members of the Panchayat|All taxpayers of the district
explanation: It is the general body that exercises direct democracy at village level.

text: The District Planning Committee is constituted to:
subject: Political Science
options: Conduct local elections|Appoint the Sarpanch|Consolidate the draft plans of Panchayats and Municipalities in the district|Audit Panchayat accounts
explanation: Article 243ZD provides for it.

text: The Gram Sabha elects the Sarpanch in every state of India.
subject: Political Science
explanation: The manner of electing the chairperson is left to the State Legislature.

text: State the main objectives of the Panchayati Raj system.
subject: Political Science
correctAnswer: Democratic decentralisation and people's participation; local planning and development; social justice through reservation; and accountability of local government to the Gram Sabha.

text: The Indus Valley Civilization was first excavated at:
subject: History
options: Harappa|Mohenjodaro|Lothal|Kalibangan
explanation: Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa in 1921.

text: The Great Bath has been found at:
subject: History
options: Dholavira|Rakhigarhi|Mohenjodaro|Harappa
explanation: It is the best known public structure of that city.

text: The Harappan port town with a dockyard is:
subject: History
options: Lothal|Kalibangan|Suktagendor|Banawali
explanation: It lies in Gujarat and points to maritime trade.

text: The Indus script has been fully deciphered.
subject: History
explanation: It remains undeciphered and no bilingual inscription has been found.

text: Which was a distinctive feature of Harappan town planning?
subject: History
options: Circular huts on hilltops|Pyramids at the city centre|Moats around every house|A grid of streets with a covered drainage system
explanation: Cities were divided into a raised citadel and a lower town.

text: The Harappan economy was based mainly on:
subject: History
options: Pastoral nomadism alone|Iron smelting|Agriculture and trade|Hunting alone
explanation: Wheat barley and cotton were grown and seals record long distance trade.

text: Harappan seals were used mainly for:
subject: History
options: Coinage|Religious sacrifice|Recording royal genealogies|Marking ownership and trade goods
explanation: Most are steatite and carry animal motifs with undeciphered script.

text: List any four features of the Indus Valley Civilization.
subject: History
correctAnswer: Planned cities with a citadel and a lower town; grid streets and covered drains; standardized burnt bricks and weights; extensive internal and external trade; the undeciphered pictographic script; bronze and copper tools with no knowledge of iron.

text: The oldest of the Vedas is the:
subject: History
options: Sama Veda|Yajur Veda|Atharva Veda|Rig Veda
explanation: It is a collection of 1028 hymns.

text: The Sama Veda is mainly a book of:
subject: History
options: Spells and charms|Historical chronicles|Chants and melodies|Ritual formulas
explanation: The origins of Indian music are traced to it.

text: The Vedic society saw the gradual development of a varna based social structure.
subject: History
explanation: The division hardened considerably in the Later Vedic period.

text: Distinguish between the Early and Later Vedic periods in the position of women.
subject: History
correctAnswer: In the Rig Vedic period women composed hymns and attended assemblies; in the Later Vedic period their position declined with child marriage and exclusion from political assemblies.

text: The first ruler of the slave dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate was:
subject: History
options: Balban|Alauddin Khalji|Qutbuddin Aibak|Iltutmish
explanation: He began the Qutb Minar and was succeeded by Iltutmish.

text: The iqta system of revenue assignment was institutionalised by:
subject: History
options: Iltutmish|Aibak|Babur|Ashoka
explanation: Land revenue assignments were given to officials in lieu of salary.

text: The Delhi Sultanate was established after the:
subject: History
options: Second battle of Tarain in 1192|First battle of Panipat in 1526|Battle of Plassey in 1757|Battle of Talikota in 1565
explanation: Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj III.

text: The Sultanate period maintained a large standing army.
subject: History
explanation: Alauddin Khalji in particular regulated market prices to sustain it.

text: The Taj Mahal was built by:
subject: History
options: Shah Jahan|Akbar|Babur|Aurangzeb
explanation: It was raised in memory of Mumtaz Mahal at Agra.

text: The mansabdari system of the Mughals determined:
subject: History
options: The caste of a soldier|The rank salary and military responsibility of an official|The land revenue rate per bigha|The order of succession to the throne
explanation: Ranks were expressed as zat and sawar.

text: Akbar's land revenue settlement based on measurement and classification was called:
subject: History
options: Chauth|Zabt or bandobast|Jizya|Iqta
explanation: Todar Mal worked it out using ten year averages of prices and yields.

text: State the main features of Mughal administration under Akbar.
subject: History
correctAnswer: A centralised monarchy with a council of ministers; the mansabdari system for civil and military ranks; the zabti land revenue settlement; provincial administration through subas; and a policy of religious tolerance including sulh-i-kul.

text: The first battle of Panipat in 1526 was fought between:
subject: History
options: Babur and Rana Sanga|Sher Shah and Humayun|Babur and Ibrahim Lodi|Akbar and Hemu
explanation: Babur's artillery and the tulghma formation decided the battle.

text: The second battle of Panipat in 1556 established:
subject: History
options: Akbar's hold over the throne of Delhi|The Delhi Sultanate|Maratha power in the north|British supremacy in Bengal
explanation: Bairam Khan led Akbar's army against Hemu.

text: Akbar's Din-i Ilahi was a syncretic faith he promoted to unite religious groups.
subject: History
explanation: It was propounded in 1582 and had very few adherents.

text: Why was the battle of Talikota of 1565 significant?
subject: History
correctAnswer: The combined Deccan sultanates decisively defeated Vijayanagara which led to the sack of Hampi and the collapse of the empire.

text: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
subject: History
subtopic: Rise of the Indian National Congress
explanation: Its first session was held at Bombay.

text: The first session of the Indian National Congress was presided over by:
subject: History
subtopic: Rise of the Indian National Congress
options: Dadabhai Naoroji|A. O. Hume|Gopal Krishna Gokhale|W. C. Bannerjee
explanation: Seventy two delegates attended it at Bombay.

text: The Moderates believed in:
subject: History
subtopic: Rise of the Indian National Congress
options: Boycott of all councils|Constitutional methods of prayer and petition|Armed revolution|Immediate complete independence
explanation: They sought self government within the Empire through gradual reform.

text: State any three contributions of the Moderate phase of the national movement.
subject: History
subtopic: Rise of the Indian National Congress
correctAnswer: An economic critique of the drain of wealth; training Indians in constitutional politics; building an all India nationalist organisation; and spreading political awareness through sessions and the press.

text: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place at:
subject: History
options: Delhi in 1911|Kanpur in 1931|Amritsar in 1919|Lahore in 1920
explanation: General Dyer fired on an unarmed crowd on 13 April 1919.

text: The Non Cooperation Movement was launched in:
subject: History
explanation: It was withdrawn after the Chauri Chaura incident in 1922.

text: The Dandi March of 1930 was part of:
subject: History
options: The Non Cooperation Movement|The Quit India Movement|The Home Rule Movement|The Civil Disobedience Movement
explanation: Gandhi marched to the sea to break the salt law.

text: Explain the main demands of the Non Cooperation Movement of 1920.
subject: History
correctAnswer: Surrender of titles and honours; boycott of government schools courts councils and foreign cloth; refusal to pay taxes; promotion of khadi and national schools; and redress of the Khilafat and Punjab wrongs leading to swaraj.

text: The Quit India Resolution was passed by the Congress in:
subject: History
options: August 1942 at Bombay|March 1930 at Karachi|December 1929 at Lahore|June 1947 at Delhi
explanation: Gandhi gave the call Do or Die.

text: The Indian National Army was led by:
subject: History
options: Vallabhbhai Patel|Maulana Azad|Subhas Chandra Bose|Bhagat Singh
explanation: It was first formed by Mohan Singh from Indian prisoners of war.

text: The Mountbatten Plan of June 1947 provided for:
subject: History
options: A confederation of princely states|Continued British rule for a decade|Partition of India and the transfer of power|Universal adult franchise alone
explanation: It led to the Indian Independence Act of July 1947.

text: Why is the Quit India Movement described as a leaderless upheaval?
subject: History
correctAnswer: All the top Congress leaders were arrested on the night of 8 August 1942 so people organised strikes sabotage and parallel governments on their own initiative.

text: The French Revolution began in the year:
subject: History
explanation: The storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 marks its beginning.

text: The American Declaration of Independence was adopted in:
subject: History
explanation: It was drafted mainly by Thomas Jefferson.

text: The slogan Liberty Equality Fraternity is associated with the:
subject: History
options: Industrial Revolution|French Revolution|Russian Revolution|Glorious Revolution
explanation: It summed up the ideals of the revolutionaries.

text: Name any two thinkers of the Enlightenment and state their ideas.
subject: History
correctAnswer: Locke argued for natural rights to life liberty and property; Montesquieu proposed the separation of powers; Rousseau held that sovereignty rests with the people; Voltaire attacked religious intolerance.

text: The Industrial Revolution began in:
subject: History
options: Britain in the late eighteenth century|France in the sixteenth century|Germany in the nineteenth century|The United States in the seventeenth century
explanation: Coal iron capital and colonial markets gave Britain the lead.

text: The invention that most transformed factory power was:
subject: History
options: The spinning jenny|The telegraph|The internal combustion engine|The improved steam engine of James Watt
explanation: It freed factories from water power sites.

text: The factory system concentrated production in one place under supervision.
subject: History
explanation: It replaced domestic and cottage production.

text: State any three social consequences of the Industrial Revolution.
subject: History
correctAnswer: Growth of crowded industrial towns; emergence of two classes the capitalists and the wage workers; long hours and child labour; the rise of trade unions and socialist ideas; and the displacement of handloom weavers.

text: The First World War began in the year:
subject: History
subtopic: World Wars and the United Nations
explanation: The immediate cause was the assassination at Sarajevo.

text: The United Nations was established in the year:
subject: History
subtopic: World Wars and the United Nations
explanation: Its Charter was signed at San Francisco.

text: The Cold War was the long standoff between:
subject: History
subtopic: World Wars and the United Nations
options: Germany and Japan|China and India|The United States and the Soviet Union|Britain and France
explanation: It was fought through proxies rather than by direct combat.

text: State any three causes of the First World War.
subject: History
subtopic: World Wars and the United Nations
correctAnswer: Militarism and an arms race; secret alliance systems dividing Europe; imperial rivalry over colonies; aggressive nationalism in the Balkans; and the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand as the immediate trigger.

text: Society is best defined as:
subject: Sociology
options: A group of people living in one building|A collection of unrelated individuals|A political organisation alone|A system of social relationships
explanation: MacIver described society as a web of social relationships.

text: A social institution is best defined as:
subject: Sociology
options: An established pattern of behaviour that meets a basic social need|A building where people work|A government department|A voluntary association
explanation: Family marriage religion and education are examples.

text: Social structure refers to the organised pattern of social relationships and institutions.
subject: Sociology
explanation: It is the relatively stable framework within which social life occurs.

text: Distinguish between society and culture.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: Society is the organised system of people and their relationships while culture is the learned way of life including beliefs customs and material objects that those people share.

text: Culture in sociology refers to:
subject: Sociology
options: The learned way of life of a society|Only classical music and art|The racial traits of a people|The economic system alone
explanation: It has material and non material elements and is transmitted by learning.

text: Socialization is the process by which a person:
subject: Sociology
options: Joins a political party|Learns and internalizes the norms and values of society|Migrates to another country|Moves up the social ladder
explanation: Family school and peer groups are its principal agents.

text: Emile Durkheim called the shared beliefs and values of a society the:
subject: Sociology
options: Social contract|Collective conscience|Class consciousness|Cultural lag
explanation: He argued that it holds society together.

text: Culture is inherited biologically from one generation to the next.
subject: Sociology
explanation: Culture is learned and socially transmitted rather than carried in the genes.

text: Who is regarded as the father of sociology?
subject: Sociology
options: Max Weber|Herbert Spencer|Auguste Comte|Karl Marx
explanation: He coined the term sociology and proposed positivism.

text: The concept of class struggle is central to the work of:
subject: Sociology
options: Karl Marx|Emile Durkheim|Auguste Comte|Talcott Parsons
explanation: He read history as the history of class struggles.

text: Verstehen or interpretive understanding was advocated by:
subject: Sociology
options: Herbert Spencer|Auguste Comte|Max Weber|Karl Marx
explanation: It means understanding social action from the actor's own point of view.

text: State the main difference between the functionalist and the conflict perspective.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: Functionalism sees society as a system of interdependent parts working together for stability while the conflict perspective sees society as an arena of inequality in which groups compete for scarce resources.

text: The family is called a primary group because its members have:
subject: Sociology
options: Formal written rules|Direct intimate and face to face relations|Only contractual relations|No emotional ties
explanation: Cooley distinguished primary from secondary groups on this basis.

text: A family consisting of a couple and their unmarried children is a:
subject: Sociology
options: Nuclear family|Joint family|Extended family|Matrilineal family
explanation: Urbanisation and industrialisation have favoured its growth.

text: The joint family in India is characterised by common property and a common kitchen.
subject: Sociology
explanation: It also involves several generations living together under one head.

text: List the main functions of the family.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: Biological reproduction and regulation of sexual behaviour; socialisation of children; economic cooperation and division of labour; emotional support and affection; and provision of social identity and status.

text: Marriage restricted to one spouse at a time is called:
subject: Sociology
options: Polyandry|Group marriage|Monogamy|Polygyny
explanation: It is the dominant form in modern societies.

text: The rule requiring marriage outside one's own group is:
subject: Sociology
options: Endogamy|Hypergamy|Homogamy|Exogamy
explanation: Endogamy is the opposite rule of marrying within the group.

text: Marriage systems studied in sociology include polygyny polyandry and monogamy.
subject: Sociology
explanation: Each carries different rules about the number and category of spouses.

text: Distinguish between endogamy and exogamy with an example from India.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: Endogamy requires marriage within a group such as caste or tribe while exogamy requires marriage outside a group such as the gotra or the village.

text: Education as a social institution functions mainly to:
subject: Sociology
options: Replace the family entirely|Regulate marriage|Transmit knowledge and socialize the young|Guarantee employment
explanation: It is a formal agent of socialisation.

text: Which is a manifest function of education?
subject: Sociology
options: Delaying entry into work|Imparting knowledge and skills|Creating a marriage market|Providing childcare
explanation: The others are latent or unintended functions.

text: Religion is a social institution that deals with the sacred.
subject: Sociology
explanation: Durkheim defined it by the division of the world into sacred and profane.

text: Explain how religion functions as an agent of social control.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: It prescribes norms and sanctions through ideas of sin and merit; it legitimises the existing social order; its rituals reinforce group solidarity; and it supplies a moral framework that guides individual conduct.

text: The caste system in India is based primarily on:
subject: Sociology
options: Birth and heredity|Wealth alone|Education|Freely chosen occupation
explanation: Membership is ascribed and normally unchangeable.

text: The concept of sanskritisation was coined by:
subject: Sociology
options: M. N. Srinivas|G. S. Ghurye|Louis Dumont|Andre Beteille
explanation: It describes a lower caste adopting the practices of a higher caste in order to rise.

text: The jajmani system refers to hereditary patron client relations between caste groups.
subject: Sociology
explanation: Service castes rendered customary services to landowning patrons.

text: State any four features of the caste system.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: Segmental division of society; a hierarchy of castes; restrictions on social intercourse and commensality; endogamy; hereditary occupation; and the civil and religious disabilities and privileges of the different castes.

text: A class differs from a caste mainly because a class is:
subject: Sociology
options: Based on birth and closed|Always hereditary|Sanctioned by religion|Based on economic position and relatively open
explanation: Mobility between classes is possible.

text: Status that a person receives at birth is called:
subject: Sociology
options: Role status|Ascribed status|Achieved status|Master status
explanation: Achieved status is earned through a person's own effort.

text: Class consciousness means awareness of shared economic interests among class members.
subject: Sociology
explanation: Marx treated it as the basis of collective class action.

text: Distinguish between caste and class.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: Caste is a closed ascribed status group based on birth with ritual sanction and endogamy; class is an open economic grouping based on income occupation and education that permits mobility and intermarriage.

text: Social mobility refers to:
subject: Sociology
options: Movement of people between social strata|Migration between villages|Growth of population|Change of religion
explanation: It may be vertical or horizontal.

text: A change from one occupation to another of the same status is:
subject: Sociology
options: Upward mobility|Intergenerational mobility|Horizontal mobility|Vertical mobility
explanation: Vertical mobility changes the level of status.

text: Mobility across generations within a family is called:
subject: Sociology
options: Structural mobility|Horizontal mobility|Intergenerational mobility|Intragenerational mobility
explanation: For example a farmer's son becoming a doctor.

text: State any three factors that promote social mobility in modern India.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: Western education and new occupations; urbanisation and industrialisation; reservation and welfare legislation; and democratic politics weakening caste restrictions on occupation.

text: Modernization in Indian society includes:
subject: Sociology
options: A strengthening of caste rules|A shift towards rational scientific and secular values|A return to subsistence farming|Rejection of all technology
explanation: Yogendra Singh studied it as a process of planned social change.

text: Development in sociology is best understood as:
subject: Sociology
options: An increase in exports only|Economic growth accompanied by social transformation|A rise in national income alone|Growth in the number of factories
explanation: It includes change in institutions welfare and the quality of life.

text: Modernisation necessarily means westernisation.
subject: Sociology
explanation: A society can adopt scientific and rational methods while retaining its own cultural identity.

text: State any three features of modernisation.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: A rational and scientific outlook; secularisation of institutions; industrialisation and urbanisation; expansion of formal education; and greater social mobility and individualism.

text: A social movement is:
subject: Sociology
options: A government scheme|A religious ritual|An organized collective effort to promote or resist social change|A random crowd
explanation: It has shared goals leadership and sustained collective action.

text: Which is an example of a peasant movement in India?
subject: Sociology
options: The Chipko movement|The Narmada Bachao Andolan|The Dalit Panthers|The Tebhaga movement
explanation: It demanded a larger share of the harvest for sharecroppers in Bengal.

text: Social movements may aim at change or at resistance to change.
subject: Sociology
explanation: Movements can be progressive reformist or revivalist.

text: Explain any three types of social movement found in India.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: Peasant and agrarian movements over land and rents; tribal movements asserting rights over forest and land; Dalit and backward class movements against caste oppression; environmental movements; women's movements; and movements of industrial workers.

text: Globalization affects society mainly through faster flows of:
subject: Sociology
options: Government orders alone|Agricultural produce alone|Local customs alone|Goods capital people and ideas
explanation: It compresses time and space in social life.

text: Economic liberalization in India was announced in:
subject: Sociology
explanation: It opened the economy to global trade and investment.

text: The green revolution in India transformed:
subject: Sociology
options: The caste system|Urban housing|The judiciary|Agricultural production through high yielding varieties
explanation: It raised wheat and rice output but widened regional and class differences.

text: State any three social consequences of globalization in India.
subject: Sociology
correctAnswer: Growth of a consumer culture and global media; new opportunities in services and migration; widening inequality between those connected to the global economy and those who are not; and pressure on traditional occupations and local cultures.

text: Psychology is the scientific study of:
subject: Psychology
options: Behaviour and mental processes|The economy|Social institutions only|The brain alone
explanation: It uses systematic observation and experiment.

text: Who established the first psychology laboratory in Leipzig in 1879?
subject: Psychology
options: Sigmund Freud|William James|Ivan Pavlov|Wilhelm Wundt
explanation: This event is usually taken as the birth of experimental psychology.

text: Structuralism studied conscious experience through:
subject: Psychology
options: Animal experiments|Case studies|Introspection|Dream analysis
explanation: Titchener tried to break consciousness into its elements.

text: State the main ideas of the functionalist school of psychology.
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: It was developed by William James and asked what the mind does rather than what it is made of; it studied the functions of consciousness in helping the organism adapt to its environment.

text: The psychoanalytic approach was founded by:
subject: Psychology
options: Abraham Maslow|Carl Rogers|Sigmund Freud|B. F. Skinner
explanation: It emphasised the unconscious mind and early childhood experience.

text: The behaviourist approach holds that psychology should study only:
subject: Psychology
options: Self actualisation|Genetic inheritance|Observable behaviour|Unconscious conflicts
explanation: Watson and Skinner were its leading figures.

text: The humanistic approach emphasizes:
subject: Psychology
options: The id ego and superego|Cognitive schemas|Personal growth and self actualisation|Conditioned reflexes
explanation: Maslow and Rogers are its main representatives.

text: The cognitive approach views the mind as an information processor.
subject: Psychology
explanation: It studies attention memory and problem solving using models of information processing.

text: The case study method involves:
subject: Psychology
options: Testing thousands of people|Manipulating a variable in a laboratory|Observing behaviour without recording it|An intensive study of one person or a small group
explanation: It gives rich detail but has limited generalisability.

text: In an experiment the variable that is manipulated is the:
subject: Psychology
options: Control variable|Independent variable|Dependent variable|Extraneous variable
explanation: The dependent variable is the one that is measured.

text: The survey method collects data from a sample using questionnaires or interviews.
subject: Psychology
explanation: Findings are generalised to the population from the sample.

text: What is the difference between naturalistic observation and controlled observation?
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: In naturalistic observation behaviour is recorded as it occurs in the real setting without interference while in controlled observation it is recorded in an arranged setting such as a laboratory where conditions can be manipulated.

text: The laws of classical conditioning were discovered by:
subject: Psychology
options: B. F. Skinner|Edward Thorndike|Albert Bandura|Ivan Pavlov
explanation: He conditioned salivation in dogs using a bell.

text: In classical conditioning the unconditioned stimulus is one that:
subject: Psychology
options: Is neutral at first|Is presented after the response|Punishes the response|Elicits a response naturally without prior learning
explanation: Food in Pavlov's experiment was the unconditioned stimulus.

text: The gradual weakening of a conditioned response when the CS is presented without the UCS is:
subject: Psychology
options: Extinction|Generalisation|Discrimination|Spontaneous recovery
explanation: After a rest period the response may reappear spontaneously.

text: State the main principles of classical conditioning.
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: Pairing a neutral stimulus with an unconditioned stimulus until the neutral stimulus alone elicits a conditioned response; acquisition extinction and spontaneous recovery; and stimulus generalisation and discrimination.

text: Operant conditioning is associated with the work of:
subject: Psychology
options: Ivan Pavlov|Wilhelm Wundt|Carl Jung|B. F. Skinner
explanation: He used a Skinner box to study rats and pigeons.

text: Positive reinforcement increases behaviour by:
subject: Psychology
options: Presenting a pleasant stimulus after the behaviour|Removing an unpleasant stimulus|Presenting an unpleasant stimulus|Withholding all consequences
explanation: Praise for completing homework is an example.

text: The law of effect was proposed by:
subject: Psychology
options: Albert Bandura|Wolfgang Kohler|Edward Thorndike|Ivan Pavlov
explanation: Behaviour followed by satisfaction tends to be repeated.

text: Punishment always produces a permanent decrease in behaviour.
subject: Psychology
explanation: Its effects are often temporary and it may produce fear aggression or avoidance of the punisher.

text: The correct order of the basic memory processes is:
subject: Psychology
options: Retrieval encoding and storage|Encoding retrieval and storage|Encoding storage and retrieval|Storage encoding and retrieval
explanation: Failure at any stage produces forgetting.

text: Sensory memory holds information for:
subject: Psychology
options: A lifetime|A fraction of a second to a few seconds|About a minute|Several hours
explanation: It is a brief register of sensory input.

text: Short term memory is also known as:
subject: Psychology
options: Procedural memory|Working memory|Long term memory|Echoic memory
explanation: Its capacity is usually taken as seven plus or minus two items.

text: Explain any three causes of forgetting.
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: Decay of the memory trace with disuse; interference from other material learned before or after; repression of unpleasant memories; retrieval failure when cues are absent; and brain injury or disease.

text: The first practical intelligence test was developed by:
subject: Psychology
options: Alfred Binet|Charles Spearman|Howard Gardner|Robert Sternberg
explanation: It was designed to identify children needing school assistance.

text: Intelligence quotient is calculated as:
subject: Psychology
options: Chronological age divided by mental age multiplied by 100|Mental age plus chronological age|Mental age multiplied by chronological age|Mental age divided by chronological age multiplied by 100
explanation: William Stern proposed the formula.

text: A child of 10 years with a mental age of 12 has an IQ of:
subject: Psychology

text: The average range of IQ in most standard tests is about 90 to 110.
subject: Psychology
explanation: Scores near 100 are the most common.

text: The two factor theory of intelligence was proposed by:
subject: Psychology
options: Charles Spearman|Louis Thurstone|Howard Gardner|J. P. Guilford
explanation: It posited a general factor g and specific factors s.

text: The theory of multiple intelligences was proposed by:
subject: Psychology
options: Lewis Terman|Howard Gardner|Charles Spearman|Alfred Binet
explanation: It includes linguistic logical musical spatial bodily and interpersonal intelligences.

text: Thurstone's theory proposed:
subject: Psychology
options: Two factor intelligence|Seven primary mental abilities|A single general factor|Three strata only
explanation: He rejected a dominant g in favour of relatively independent abilities.

text: Compare Spearman's and Gardner's views of intelligence.
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: Spearman treated intelligence as one general ability plus specific abilities measured by tests while Gardner proposed several relatively independent intelligences of which logical and linguistic abilities are only two.

text: Emotional intelligence refers to the ability to:
subject: Psychology
options: Solve arithmetic problems quickly|Recall facts accurately|Score highly on IQ tests|Recognise understand and manage one's own and others' emotions
explanation: Salovey and Mayer introduced the concept and Goleman popularised it.

text: Aptitude refers to a person's:
subject: Psychology
options: Interest in a hobby|Emotional stability|Potential to learn a particular skill|Current level of achievement
explanation: Aptitude tests predict future performance.

text: An achievement test measures what a person has already learned.
subject: Psychology
explanation: An aptitude test by contrast predicts what a person could learn.

text: State any four components of emotional intelligence.
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: Self awareness of one's emotions; self regulation of impulses and moods; motivation and persistence; empathy for others' feelings; and social skills for managing relationships.

text: Mental health is best described as:
subject: Psychology
options: Physical fitness alone|A state of wellbeing in which a person copes with the normal stresses of life|The absence of any emotion|A high score on an intelligence test
explanation: The WHO definition includes the ability to work productively.

text: Disorders marked by excessive fear and apprehension are called:
subject: Psychology
options: Anxiety disorders|Mood disorders|Personality disorders|Psychotic disorders
explanation: Phobias and panic disorder belong to this group.

text: Which is classified as a psychotic disorder?
subject: Psychology
options: Obsessive compulsive disorder|Anorexia nervosa|Generalised anxiety disorder|Schizophrenia
explanation: It involves delusions hallucinations and a loss of contact with reality.

text: Mental disorders are caused only by weak character.
subject: Psychology
explanation: They arise from an interaction of biological psychological and social factors.

text: Psychoanalysis uses which technique to bring unconscious material into awareness?
subject: Psychology
options: Systematic desensitisation|Token economy|Electroconvulsive therapy|Free association
explanation: Dream interpretation and analysis of resistance are also used.

text: Cognitive behaviour therapy aims to:
subject: Psychology
options: Uncover childhood conflicts only|Prescribe medication|Explore the collective unconscious|Change maladaptive thoughts and behaviours
explanation: Aaron Beck developed the cognitive form of this therapy.

text: Client centred therapy was developed by:
subject: Psychology
options: B. F. Skinner|Fritz Perls|Carl Rogers|Sigmund Freud
explanation: It stresses unconditional positive regard and empathy.

text: Distinguish between psychotherapy and biomedical therapy.
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: Psychotherapy uses psychological methods such as talking insight and behaviour change while biomedical therapy uses drugs and other physiological treatments directed at the nervous system.

text: Hans Selye described the body's reaction to stress as:
subject: Psychology
options: Cognitive dissonance|Learned helplessness|The general adaptation syndrome|The relaxation response
explanation: It has three stages of alarm resistance and exhaustion.

text: Problem focused coping involves:
subject: Psychology
options: Taking direct action to change the source of stress|Avoiding the situation|Denying the problem|Seeking emotional comfort only
explanation: Emotion focused coping regulates the feelings attached to the stressor.

text: Which of these is a healthy way to reduce stress?
subject: Psychology
options: Substance use|Regular physical exercise|Excessive caffeine intake|Social withdrawal
explanation: Exercise lowers physiological arousal and improves mood.

text: State any four techniques used to cope with stress.
subject: Psychology
correctAnswer: Relaxation and breathing exercises; regular physical activity; time management and realistic goal setting; social support from family and friends; and cognitive restructuring of negative thoughts.

text: A function f is continuous at x = a if the limit of f(x) as x approaches a equals f(a). This statement is:
subject: Mathematics
explanation: All three conditions: f(a) exists; the limit exists; and the two are equal.

text: The intermediate value theorem requires the function to be:
subject: Mathematics
options: Continuous on a closed interval|Differentiable|Increasing|Periodic
explanation: A continuous function takes every value between its endpoint values.

text: State the definition of continuity of a function at a point.
subject: Mathematics
correctAnswer: The function is continuous at a point if the limit as x approaches the point exists and is equal to the value of the function at that point.

text: The derivative of x cubed is:
subject: Mathematics
options: 3 x|x cubed / 3|x squared|3 x squared
explanation: Apply the power rule: bring down the exponent and reduce it by one.

text: The derivative of sin x is:
subject: Mathematics
options: -sin x|tan x|cos x|-cos x
explanation: The derivative of cos x is -sin x which is the companion result.

text: The chain rule states that the derivative of f(g(x)) equals f prime of g(x) times g prime of x. This statement is:
subject: Mathematics
explanation: Differentiate the outer function keeping the inner intact then multiply by the inner derivative.

text: At a local maximum of a differentiable function the derivative equals zero. This statement is:
subject: Mathematics
explanation: Fermat's theorem: an interior extremum of a differentiable function has a horizontal tangent.

text: State the product rule for differentiation.
subject: Mathematics
correctAnswer: The derivative of the product f g is f prime g plus f g prime.

text: The integral of 2x dx is:
subject: Mathematics
options: 2 x squared + C|x + C|2 + C|x squared + C
explanation: Differentiating x squared + C gives back 2x.

text: The fundamental theorem of calculus connects differentiation and integration. This statement is:
subject: Mathematics
explanation: It shows that integration is the inverse of differentiation and gives the evaluation rule for definite integrals.

text: The definite integral of 3x squared from 0 to 1 equals:
subject: Mathematics
explanation: An antiderivative is x cubed; evaluating from 0 to 1 gives 1 - 0.

text: Explain what an indefinite integral means.
subject: Mathematics
correctAnswer: It denotes the family of all antiderivatives of a function; any two members differ by a constant C.

text: The order of a differential equation is the:
subject: Mathematics
options: Degree of the highest derivative|Highest order derivative present|Number of independent variables|Power of x
explanation: An equation with y prime prime is of second order.

text: The general solution of dy/dx = y is:
subject: Mathematics
options: y = sin x|y = C e to the x|y = ln x|y = x squared
explanation: Separate variables: dy/y = dx; integrate to get ln|y| = x + C.

text: An equation of the form dy/dx + P(x) y = Q(x) is a first order linear ordinary differential equation. This statement is:
subject: Mathematics
explanation: It is solved using an integrating factor.

text: The integrating factor for dy/dx + P(x) y = Q(x) is e to the integral of P dx. This statement is:
subject: Mathematics
explanation: Multiplying through makes the left side the derivative of a product.

text: Define the order and degree of a differential equation.
subject: Mathematics
correctAnswer: The order is the highest derivative present; the degree is the power of that highest derivative when the equation is a polynomial in its derivatives.

text: The splitting of white light into its colours is called:
subject: Physics
options: Emission|Reflection|Dispersion|Absorption
explanation: Different wavelengths bend by different amounts in a prism.

text: Young's double slit experiment demonstrates the:
subject: Physics
options: Particle nature of light|Wave nature of light through interference|Gravitation of light|Charge of light
explanation: The alternating bright and dark fringes come from constructive and destructive interference.

text: The focal length of a plane mirror is infinite. This statement is:
subject: Physics
explanation: Its reflecting surface has no curvature so the focal length is taken as infinity.

text: State Huygens' principle.
subject: Physics
correctAnswer: Every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets and the new wavefront is the envelope of those wavelets.

text: The SI unit of electrical resistance is the:
subject: Physics
options: Volt|Ampere|Ohm|Watt
explanation: One ohm is the resistance that allows one ampere under one volt.

text: Ohm's law holds exactly when the:
subject: Physics
options: Circuit is open|Voltage is changing rapidly|Temperature is kept constant|Current is zero
explanation: V = I R for ohmic conductors at constant temperature.

text: The magnetic force on a moving charge is given by F = q v cross B. This statement is:
subject: Physics
explanation: The force is perpendicular to both the velocity and the field and equals q v B sin theta.

text: State Kirchhoff's junction rule.
subject: Physics
correctAnswer: The total current entering a junction equals the total current leaving it; it is a statement of conservation of charge.

text: The photoelectric effect was explained by:
subject: Physics
options: Niels Bohr alone|James Maxwell|Isaac Newton|Albert Einstein
explanation: Einstein showed that light comes in quanta (photons) of energy h f; he won the Nobel Prize for this.

text: The energy of a photon is given by:
subject: Physics
options: E = m v squared|E = h f / c|E = h f|E = m c squared only
explanation: Energy is proportional to the frequency of the radiation.

text: In the Bohr model electrons occupy stationary orbits with quantized angular momentum. This statement is:
subject: Physics
explanation: An electron radiates energy only when it jumps between allowed orbits.

text: The energy released in the fission of uranium 235 comes from the mass defect converted by E = m c squared. This statement is:
subject: Physics
explanation: The products weigh slightly less than the reactants and the lost mass appears as energy.

text: State Heisenberg's uncertainty principle.
subject: Physics
correctAnswer: The product of the uncertainties in position and momentum is at least h over 4 pi; the two cannot be known exactly at the same time.

text: The first law of thermodynamics is a statement of:
subject: Physics
options: Conservation of energy|Newton's first law|Ohm's law|Increase of entropy
explanation: Energy can change form but the total energy of an isolated system is constant.

text: In an isothermal process the:
subject: Physics
options: Temperature is constant|Volume is constant|Pressure is constant|Heat exchange is zero
explanation: For an ideal gas internal energy depends only on temperature so delta U is zero in an isothermal change.

text: The efficiency of a Carnot engine depends only on the temperatures of the source and the sink. This statement is:
subject: Physics
explanation: No real engine can exceed the Carnot efficiency for the same reservoirs.

text: Absolute zero is:
subject: Physics
options: 100 kelvin|-100 degrees Celsius|0 degrees Celsius|0 kelvin (about -273.15 degrees Celsius)
explanation: It is the lower limit of the thermodynamic temperature scale.

text: State the second law of thermodynamics in the Clausius form.
subject: Physics
correctAnswer: Heat cannot of itself pass from a colder body to a hotter body; external work is required for refrigeration.

text: The bond formed by the sharing of electron pairs is the:
subject: Chemistry
options: Ionic bond|Covalent bond|Metallic bond|Hydrogen bond
explanation: Atoms share pairs to complete their valence shells.

text: The VSEPR theory predicts molecular shape from the:
subject: Chemistry
options: Colour of the compound|Repulsion of electron pairs around the central atom|Mass of the central atom|Charge of the nucleus only
explanation: Electron pairs arrange themselves as far apart as possible.

text: Among H2O; H2S; HCl; and CH4 the strongest hydrogen bonding is shown by water. This statement is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Oxygen is small and highly electronegative so O-H-O hydrogen bonds are strong.

text: Distinguish between an ionic bond and a covalent bond.
subject: Chemistry
correctAnswer: An ionic bond involves transfer of electrons between metal and non metal with electrostatic attraction and high melting points; a covalent bond involves sharing of electron pairs usually between non metals with lower melting points.

text: The entropy of a system increases when its disorder increases. This statement is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Gases have higher entropy than liquids which have higher entropy than solids.

text: The enthalpy change of a reaction depends only on the initial and final states. This statement is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Enthalpy is a state function; this is the basis of Hess's law.

text: The device that converts chemical energy into electrical energy is:
subject: Chemistry
options: A capacitor|An electrolytic cell|A galvanic (voltaic) cell|A transformer
explanation: A spontaneous redox reaction drives the current in a galvanic cell.

text: The Nernst equation is used to calculate the cell potential under non standard conditions. This statement is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: It relates potential to the activities (concentrations) of the reacting species.

text: Corrosion of iron is essentially an electrochemical oxidation process. This statement is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Iron acts as an anode and loses electrons in the presence of moisture and oxygen.

text: State Faraday's first law of electrolysis.
subject: Chemistry
correctAnswer: The mass of a substance deposited or liberated at an electrode is proportional to the quantity of electricity that passes through the electrolyte: m = Z I t.

text: The central metal ion in the complex [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 is:
subject: Chemistry
options: Nitrogen|Chlorine|Cobalt|Ammonia
explanation: Six ammonia ligands are coordinated to the cobalt inside the brackets.

text: The coordination number of the complex ion [Fe(CN)6] 3- is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: It equals the number of donor atoms bonded to the central metal; here six cyanide carbons.

text: Ammonia acts as a monodentate ligand. This statement is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: It donates a single lone pair from the nitrogen atom.

text: The complex [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 dissociates in solution into one complex cation and three chloride ions. This statement is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: The ions inside the coordination sphere do not ionize; the counter ions do.

text: Define a ligand and a coordination entity.
subject: Chemistry
correctAnswer: A ligand is an ion or molecule that donates a lone pair of electrons to a metal; the coordination entity is the central metal with its ligands enclosed in brackets.

text: In Python which of the following is an immutable data type:
subject: Computer Science
options: set|list|tuple|dict
explanation: Once created a tuple's elements cannot be changed.

text: An infinite loop occurs when the loop condition never becomes false. This statement is:
subject: Computer Science
explanation: A missing or wrong update of the loop variable is the most common cause.

text: Distinguish between a compiler and an interpreter.
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: A compiler translates the whole source program into machine code before execution; an interpreter executes the source line by line at run time.

text: A stack follows the:
subject: Computer Science
options: LIFO principle|Random access principle|Priority principle|FIFO principle
explanation: The last element pushed is the first one popped.

text: A queue follows the FIFO principle. This statement is:
subject: Computer Science
explanation: The first element enqueued is the first one dequeued; it models waiting lines.

text: In a binary search tree the left child of a node holds keys:
subject: Computer Science
options: Smaller than the node|Equal to the node|Always null|Larger than the node
explanation: This ordering makes search traverse one side at a time.

text: The average time complexity of a hash table lookup with a good hash function is O(1). This statement is:
subject: Computer Science
explanation: Collisions degrade the worst case but the average stays constant for a good load factor.

text: State three applications of a stack.
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: Managing function calls (the call stack); evaluating arithmetic expressions; and matching brackets in code.

text: In a relational database a table is a:
subject: Computer Science
options: Class|Pointer|File|Relation
explanation: Rows are tuples and columns are attributes of the relation.

text: The SQL command used to retrieve data is:
subject: Computer Science
options: DELETE|INSERT|SELECT|UPDATE
explanation: SELECT specifies which columns and which rows to return.

text: The primary key of a table must be unique and not null. This statement is:
subject: Computer Science
explanation: It uniquely identifies every row of the table.

text: Normalization is used to reduce redundancy and update anomalies. This statement is:
subject: Computer Science
explanation: Each form of normal form removes a specific kind of dependency problem.

text: Explain what a foreign key is.
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: A foreign key is a column or set of columns in one table that references the primary key of another table; it enforces the relationship between the two tables.

text: The process of switching the CPU between running processes is called:
subject: Computer Science
options: Printing|Compiling|Booting|Context switching
explanation: The saved state of one process is stored and the state of the next is restored.

text: The four Coffman conditions for deadlock are mutual exclusion; hold and wait; no preemption; and circular wait. This statement is:
subject: Computer Science
explanation: All four must hold simultaneously for deadlock to occur; removing any one prevents it.

text: Virtual memory allows processes to use disk space as an extension of RAM. This statement is:
subject: Computer Science
explanation: The page table maps virtual pages to physical frames and pages out rarely used pages.

text: List the four Coffman conditions required for deadlock.
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: Mutual exclusion; hold and wait; no preemption; and circular wait.

text: The limit of (x squared - 1) / (x - 1) as x approaches 1 is:
subject: Mathematics
explanation: (x squared - 1)/(x - 1) = x + 1 and substituting x = 1 gives 2.

text: The limit of a function at a point describes:
subject: Mathematics
options: The slope of the graph|The area under the curve|The maximum value of the function|The value the function approaches as x gets close to that point
explanation: The limit need not equal the value of the function at that point.

text: If the left hand limit and the right hand limit at a point are unequal then:
subject: Mathematics
options: The function is continuous|The limit does not exist|The limit is their average|The limit is the larger one
explanation: Both one sided limits must exist and be equal for the limit to exist.

text: A limit can exist at a point where the function is not defined.
subject: Mathematics
explanation: The definition of a limit depends only on values near the point and not at it.

text: A function f is continuous at x = a when:
subject: Mathematics
options: The limit as x approaches a equals f(a)|f(a) is the largest value of f|The derivative at a is zero|f is defined for all real numbers
explanation: This requires f(a) to exist the limit to exist and the two to be equal.

text: Which function is discontinuous at x = 0?
subject: Mathematics
options: f(x) = x squared|f(x) = sin x|f(x) = x + 3|f(x) = 1 / x
explanation: It tends to infinity as x approaches zero so the limit does not exist.

text: Every polynomial function is continuous at every real number.
subject: Mathematics
explanation: Polynomials have no breaks jumps or holes on the real line.

text: State the three conditions for the continuity of a function at a point.
subject: Mathematics
correctAnswer: f(a) must be defined; the limit of f(x) as x approaches a must exist; and that limit must equal f(a).

text: The limit of (sin x) / x as x approaches 0 is:
subject: Mathematics
explanation: This is a standard limit proved geometrically using the sandwich theorem.

text: The limit of (1 + 1/n) raised to the power n as n approaches infinity is:
subject: Mathematics
options: 0|infinity|e|1
explanation: This is the standard definition of the number e.

text: The intermediate value theorem applies to functions that are:
subject: Mathematics
options: Continuous on a closed interval|Differentiable everywhere|Bounded and monotonic|Defined only at rational points
explanation: It guarantees every intermediate value is attained on that interval.

text: The sandwich theorem is used to evaluate limits by bounding a function between two others.
subject: Mathematics
explanation: If both bounding functions have the same limit the middle one must have it too.

text: The derivative of x cubed from first principles is:
subject: Mathematics
options: 3x|x cubed divided by 3|3 x squared|x squared
explanation: Expanding (x + h) cubed and letting h tend to zero leaves 3 x squared.

text: The derivative from first principles is defined as the limit of:
subject: Mathematics
options: h divided by f(x)|f(x + h) - f(x) all over h as h approaches 0|f(x) times h|f(x + h) plus f(x)
explanation: It measures the instantaneous rate of change.

text: The derivative of sin x from first principles is:
subject: Mathematics
options: tan x|cos x|-sin x|-cos x
explanation: It follows by expanding sin(x + h) and using standard limits.

text: Geometrically the derivative at a point gives the slope of the tangent there.
subject: Mathematics
explanation: The tangent line at x = a has slope f'(a).

text: The derivative of a product of two functions is given by the:
subject: Mathematics
options: Product rule|Chain rule|Quotient rule|Mean value theorem
explanation: d(uv)/dx = u dv/dx + v du/dx.

text: The chain rule is used when differentiating:
subject: Mathematics
options: A sum of two functions|An implicit relation only|A composite function|A constant function
explanation: dy/dx = dy/du times du/dx.

text: The derivative of e raised to 2x with respect to x is:
subject: Mathematics
options: e raised to 2x|2x e raised to 2x|e raised to x|2 e raised to 2x
explanation: The chain rule multiplies by the derivative of the inner function 2x.

text: Differentiate y = x squared times sin x using the product rule.
subject: Mathematics
correctAnswer: dy/dx = x squared cos x + 2x sin x.

text: At a local maximum of a differentiable function the first derivative is:
subject: Mathematics
options: Negative|Undefined|Zero|Positive
explanation: Such points are called stationary or critical points.

text: If the derivative equals zero and the second derivative is negative at a point then the point is a:
subject: Mathematics
options: Point of inflection|Vertical asymptote|Local maximum|Local minimum
explanation: A positive second derivative would indicate a local minimum.

text: A function is strictly increasing on an interval when its derivative there is:
subject: Mathematics
options: Positive|Zero|Negative|Constant
explanation: The graph rises as x increases.

text: Find the stationary points of f(x) = x cubed - 3x and classify them.
subject: Mathematics
correctAnswer: f'(x) = 3x squared - 3 = 0 gives x = 1 and x = -1. The second derivative 6x is positive at x = 1 so it is a local minimum and negative at x = -1 so it is a local maximum.

text: The indefinite integral of 2x with respect to x is:
subject: Mathematics
options: 2 + C|x squared + C|2 x squared + C|x + C
explanation: The constant C appears because any constant differentiates to zero.

text: The integral of 1 / x dx is:
subject: Mathematics
options: 1 / x squared + C|e raised to x + C|log x absolute value + C|x log x + C
explanation: It is a standard result valid for x not equal to zero.

text: Integration is the reverse process of differentiation.
subject: Mathematics
explanation: For this reason it is also called antidifferentiation.

text: Evaluate the indefinite integral of (3 x squared + 2x) dx.
subject: Mathematics

text: Which technique is used to integrate a product of an algebraic and a trigonometric function?
subject: Mathematics
options: Completing the square|Substitution of x = 1/t|Integration by parts|Partial fractions
explanation: The formula comes from the product rule of differentiation.

text: The method of partial fractions is used to integrate:
subject: Mathematics
options: Trigonometric identities|Exponential products|Logarithmic derivatives|Rational functions
explanation: The rational function is first decomposed into simpler fractions.

text: Integration by substitution reverses which rule of differentiation?
subject: Mathematics
options: The power rule|The chain rule|The product rule|The quotient rule
explanation: The inner function is replaced by a new variable.

text: State the formula for integration by parts.
subject: Mathematics
correctAnswer: The integral of u dv = uv - the integral of v du where u and v are functions of x.

text: The definite integral of 3x squared dx from 0 to 2 equals:
subject: Mathematics
explanation: The antiderivative is x cubed and 2 cubed - 0 cubed = 8.

text: The fundamental theorem of calculus connects:
subject: Mathematics
options: Limits and continuity|Algebra and geometry|Sequences and series|Differentiation and integration
explanation: It states that integration of a derivative returns the original function.

text: A definite integral represents geometrically:
subject: Mathematics
options: The length of the curve only|The volume of revolution only|The signed area between the curve and the x axis|The slope of the tangent
explanation: Areas below the axis count as negative.

text: The value of a definite integral changes when the variable of integration is renamed.
subject: Mathematics
explanation: The variable is a dummy variable so the value is unaffected.

text: The order of a differential equation is:
subject: Mathematics
options: The order of the highest derivative present|The highest power of the unknown function|The number of terms|The power of the highest derivative
explanation: The degree is the power of the highest order derivative once the equation is polynomial.

text: What are the order and degree of d squared y / dx squared + (dy/dx) cubed = 0?
subject: Mathematics
options: Order 1 and degree 2|Order 3 and degree 2|Order 2 and degree 1|Order 2 and degree 3
explanation: The highest derivative is second order and it appears to the first power.

text: A differential equation is formed by eliminating arbitrary constants from a family of curves.
subject: Mathematics
explanation: The number of constants eliminated gives the order of the equation.

text: Form the differential equation of the family of straight lines y = mx + c.
subject: Mathematics
correctAnswer: Differentiating twice gives d squared y / dx squared = 0 since both m and c are eliminated.

text: A first order linear differential equation has the standard form:
subject: Mathematics
options: d squared y / dx squared = 0|dy/dx + y squared = 0|dy/dx + P(x) y = Q(x)|dy/dx = y squared
explanation: P and Q are functions of x alone.

text: The integrating factor of dy/dx + P y = Q is:
subject: Mathematics
options: log P|P divided by Q|e raised to the integral of P dx|The integral of P dx
explanation: Multiplying through by it makes the left side an exact derivative.

text: Solve dy/dx = y given y(0) = 1.
subject: Mathematics
explanation: Separating variables gives log y = x + C and y(0) = 1 gives C = 0 so y = e raised to x.

text: The equation dy/dx = y / x is solved by separating the variables.
subject: Mathematics
explanation: It gives log y = log x + C so y = Cx.

text: The general solution of a second order linear homogeneous equation contains:
subject: Mathematics
options: One arbitrary constant|No arbitrary constants|Three arbitrary constants|Two arbitrary constants
explanation: The number of constants equals the order of the equation.

text: The complementary function of d squared y / dx squared - 4y = 0 is:
subject: Mathematics
options: C1 e raised to 4x|C1 sin 2x + C2 cos 2x|C1 x + C2|C1 e raised to 2x + C2 e raised to -2x
explanation: The auxiliary equation m squared - 4 = 0 has roots 2 and -2.

text: Which is a real world application of differential equations?
subject: Mathematics
options: Solving a system of linear equations by elimination|Modelling population growth|Computing the mean of a data set|Drawing a histogram
explanation: Exponential growth and decay laws are written as differential equations.

text: Explain the difference between a general solution and a particular solution.
subject: Mathematics
correctAnswer: The general solution contains arbitrary constants and represents the whole family of solutions while a particular solution is obtained from it by applying initial or boundary conditions.

text: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
subject: Physics
explanation: 3 x 10 raised to 8 metres per second.

text: Huygens principle states that every point on a wavefront acts as:
subject: Physics
options: A point of maximum intensity|A reflector of the wave|A source of secondary wavelets|A node of zero amplitude
explanation: The new wavefront is the envelope of these secondary wavelets.

text: The speed of a wave equals the product of its frequency and wavelength.
subject: Physics
explanation: v = f times lambda for all periodic waves.

text: Explain how Huygens principle accounts for refraction.
subject: Physics
correctAnswer: When a plane wavefront enters a denser medium the secondary wavelets on that side travel more slowly so the wavefront bends towards the normal giving Snell's law.

text: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
subject: Physics
options: Virtual erect and of the same size|Real and inverted|Magnified and virtual|Diminished and real
explanation: It is laterally inverted and lies as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

text: Snell's law of refraction relates:
subject: Physics
options: Intensity to distance|The sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction|The angles of reflection only|Frequency to wavelength
explanation: The ratio of the sines is the refractive index of the second medium.

text: The splitting of white light into colours by a prism is called:
subject: Physics
options: Polarisation|Interference|Dispersion|Diffraction
explanation: It happens because the refractive index depends on wavelength.

text: The mirror used as a rear view mirror in vehicles is:
subject: Physics
options: Plane|Parabolic|Convex|Concave
explanation: It gives an erect diminished image with a wide field of view.

text: Young's double slit experiment demonstrates:
subject: Physics
options: The photoelectric effect|Total internal reflection|The wave nature of light|The particle nature of light
explanation: It produced a pattern of bright and dark fringes.

text: In the double slit experiment bright fringes occur where the path difference is:
subject: Physics
options: Always zero|A quarter wavelength|A whole number multiple of the wavelength|An odd multiple of half the wavelength
explanation: Constructive interference needs a path difference of n lambda.

text: Diffraction is the bending of light around the edges of an obstacle.
subject: Physics
explanation: It is most pronounced when the obstacle is comparable in size to the wavelength.

text: State the conditions required for sustained interference of light.
subject: Physics
correctAnswer: The two sources must be coherent with a constant phase difference; they should be monochromatic; their amplitudes should be nearly equal; and they must be close together.

text: Ohm's law states that at constant temperature the current through a conductor is:
subject: Physics
options: Directly proportional to the potential difference across it|Inversely proportional to the potential difference|Independent of the potential difference|Equal to the resistance
explanation: V = IR where R is the constant of proportionality.

text: The unit of electrical resistance is the:
subject: Physics
options: Watt|Ohm|Volt|Ampere
explanation: One ohm equals one volt per ampere.

text: Kirchhoff's junction rule is a statement of the conservation of:
subject: Physics
options: Momentum|Mass|Charge|Energy
explanation: The loop rule on the other hand follows from conservation of energy.

text: A current of 2 amperes flows through a resistance of 5 ohms. The potential difference is:
subject: Physics
explanation: V = IR = 2 x 5 = 10 volts.

text: Coulomb's law states that the force between two point charges varies:
subject: Physics
options: Inversely as the distance|Independently of the distance|Inversely as the square of the distance between them|Directly as the square of the distance
explanation: It is directly proportional to the product of the charges.

text: The unit of capacitance is the:
subject: Physics
options: Ohm|Coulomb|Farad|Henry
explanation: One farad is one coulomb per volt.

text: Electric field lines never intersect each other.
subject: Physics
explanation: If they did the field would have two directions at the point of intersection.

text: Two capacitors of 4 microfarad and 6 microfarad are connected in parallel. The equivalent capacitance is:
subject: Physics
explanation: Capacitances in parallel add so 4 + 6 = 10 microfarad.

text: The magnetic force on a moving charge is given by:
subject: Physics
options: q times E|q divided by v|m times a|q times v cross B
explanation: It is perpendicular to both the velocity and the field.

text: The unit of inductance is the:
subject: Physics
options: Henry|Farad|Tesla|Weber
explanation: The unit of magnetic flux density is the tesla and of flux the weber.

text: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced emf equals:
subject: Physics
options: The rate of change of charge|The negative rate of change of magnetic flux|The magnetic flux itself|The product of flux and current
explanation: The negative sign is Lenz's law and shows that the induced emf opposes the change.

text: State Lenz's law and explain what it is a consequence of.
subject: Physics
correctAnswer: The direction of the induced current is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it. It is a consequence of the conservation of energy.

text: In the photoelectric effect the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons depends on:
subject: Physics
options: The intensity of the incident light|The duration of exposure|The area of the metal plate|The frequency of the incident light
explanation: Intensity affects only the number of electrons emitted.

text: The minimum frequency of light needed to eject electrons from a metal is called the:
subject: Physics
options: Stopping potential|Threshold frequency|Cut off wavelength|Work function
explanation: Below it no emission occurs however intense the light.

text: The energy of a photon of frequency f is:
subject: Physics
options: h divided by f|f divided by h|h times f squared|h times f
explanation: h is Planck's constant with value 6.626 x 10 raised to -34 joule second.

text: Einstein explained the photoelectric effect by treating light as a stream of particles called photons.
subject: Physics
explanation: He received the Nobel Prize in 1921 for this work.

text: In the Bohr model electrons revolve in:
subject: Physics
options: Orbits that decay continuously|Certain allowed stationary orbits without radiating energy|Any orbit they choose|A single fixed orbit only
explanation: Radiation is emitted only when an electron jumps between these orbits.

text: The angular momentum of an electron in the nth Bohr orbit is quantised in multiples of:
subject: Physics
options: 2 pi h|h divided by 4 pi|h divided by 2 pi|h
explanation: L = n h / 2 pi is Bohr's quantisation condition.

text: The Rutherford scattering experiment led to the discovery of:
subject: Physics
options: The electron|The neutron|The proton charge|The atomic nucleus
explanation: Most alpha particles passed straight through showing the atom is mostly empty space.

text: The Balmer series of the hydrogen spectrum lies in the:
subject: Physics
options: Infrared region|X ray region|Visible region|Ultraviolet region
explanation: The Lyman series is ultraviolet and the Paschen series infrared.

text: The fission of uranium 235 is usually initiated by:
subject: Physics
options: A gamma photon|An alpha particle|A slow neutron|A fast proton
explanation: It releases further neutrons making a chain reaction possible.

text: The energy released in a nuclear reaction comes from:
subject: Physics
options: The mass defect converted according to E = m c squared|Chemical bond breaking|Electron transitions|Friction between nucleons
explanation: The mass defect is the difference between the sum of the nucleon masses and the nuclear mass.

text: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle states that:
subject: Physics
options: Energy is always conserved|Electrons move in fixed orbits|Light is only a wave|Position and momentum cannot both be measured exactly at the same time
explanation: The product of the uncertainties is at least h / 4 pi.

text: Nuclear fusion releases energy by combining light nuclei into heavier ones.
subject: Physics
explanation: It powers the sun and needs extremely high temperatures.

text: The first law of thermodynamics is a statement of the conservation of:
subject: Physics
options: Mass|Momentum|Charge|Energy
explanation: It is written as dQ = dU + dW.

text: In an isothermal process of an ideal gas the quantity that remains constant is:
subject: Physics
options: Entropy|Temperature|Pressure|Volume
explanation: An adiabatic process keeps heat exchange zero and an isobaric one keeps pressure constant.

text: For an isochoric process the work done by the gas is:
subject: Physics
explanation: The volume does not change so P dV = 0 and all the heat raises the internal energy.

text: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on its temperature.
subject: Physics
explanation: It is independent of pressure and volume for an ideal gas.

text: The second law of thermodynamics implies that heat cannot:
subject: Physics
options: Be converted into work at all|Exist in a reversible process|Flow by itself from a colder to a hotter body|Flow from hot to cold
explanation: This is the Clausius statement of the law.

text: Entropy is a measure of:
subject: Physics
options: The pressure of a gas|The volume of a container|The disorder or randomness of a system|The temperature of a system
explanation: In an isolated system it never decreases.

text: The efficiency of any heat engine can reach one hundred percent.
subject: Physics
explanation: The Kelvin Planck statement forbids converting all absorbed heat into work in a cycle.

text: State the Kelvin Planck statement of the second law.
subject: Physics
correctAnswer: No heat engine operating in a cycle can convert the whole of the heat absorbed from a single reservoir into work without rejecting some heat to a colder reservoir.

text: The Carnot engine is an ideal reversible engine working between:
subject: Physics
options: Two heat reservoirs at different temperatures|A single reservoir|Three reservoirs|Reservoirs at equal temperature
explanation: Its cycle has two isothermal and two adiabatic stages.

text: The efficiency of a Carnot engine depends only on:
subject: Physics
options: The working substance|The size of the engine|The pressure of the gas|The temperatures of the source and the sink
explanation: Efficiency = 1 - T sink / T source.

text: Absolute zero on the Kelvin scale is:
subject: Physics
explanation: Zero kelvin equals minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.

text: A Carnot engine operates between 400 K and 300 K. Its efficiency in percent is:
subject: Physics

text: A covalent bond is formed by:
subject: Chemistry
options: Hydrogen attraction alone|The sharing of electron pairs between atoms|The transfer of electrons|The attraction between a sea of electrons and cations
explanation: It usually forms between non metal atoms.

text: An ionic bond forms between atoms whose electronegativity difference is:
subject: Chemistry
options: Large usually greater than 1.7|Very small|Exactly zero|Always less than 0.5
explanation: Electrons are transferred from the metal to the non metal.

text: Which compound contains an ionic bond?
subject: Chemistry
options: Water|Sodium chloride|Hydrogen chloride|Methane
explanation: It consists of Na+ and Cl- ions held together electrostatically.

text: Ionic compounds conduct electricity in the solid state.
subject: Chemistry
explanation: The ions are fixed in a lattice; they conduct only when molten or in solution.

text: The shape of the methane molecule is:
subject: Chemistry
options: Octahedral|Tetrahedral|Trigonal planar|Linear
explanation: Four bond pairs arrange themselves at 109.5 degrees.

text: VSEPR theory predicts molecular shape based on:
subject: Chemistry
options: The mass of the atoms|The number of protons|The colour of the compound|Repulsion between valence shell electron pairs
explanation: Electron pairs arrange themselves as far apart as possible.

text: Water is bent rather than linear because it has:
subject: Chemistry
options: Two lone pairs on the oxygen|No lone pairs|Four bond pairs|An ionic bond
explanation: Lone pair repulsion compresses the bond angle to about 104.5 degrees.

text: State the shape and bond angle of ammonia using VSEPR theory.
subject: Chemistry
correctAnswer: Ammonia has three bond pairs and one lone pair so it is pyramidal with a bond angle of about 107 degrees.

text: Hydrogen bonding occurs when hydrogen is bonded to an atom that is:
subject: Chemistry
options: Highly electronegative such as fluorine oxygen or nitrogen|A metal|Positively charged|In the same period
explanation: The electronegative atom pulls electron density away from the hydrogen.

text: Which intermolecular force is the weakest?
subject: Chemistry
options: Hydrogen bonds|Dipole dipole forces|Ion dipole forces|London dispersion forces
explanation: They arise from temporary fluctuations in electron density.

text: The unusually high boiling point of water is due to:
subject: Chemistry
options: Extensive hydrogen bonding|Its ionic character|London forces alone|Its low molecular mass
explanation: More energy is needed to separate the molecules.

text: Hydrogen bonding explains why ice floats on water.
subject: Chemistry
explanation: The open hydrogen bonded lattice makes ice less dense than liquid water.

text: Enthalpy change of a reaction is defined at:
subject: Chemistry
options: Constant entropy|Constant pressure|Constant volume|Constant temperature only
explanation: At constant pressure the heat exchanged equals the change in enthalpy.

text: Hess's law states that the enthalpy change of a reaction depends only on:
