subject: Chemistry
options: The initial and final states|The path followed|The number of steps|The catalyst used
explanation: It follows from enthalpy being a state function.

text: An exothermic reaction has a:
subject: Chemistry
options: Enthalpy change equal to entropy|Negative enthalpy change|Positive enthalpy change|Zero enthalpy change
explanation: Heat is released to the surroundings.

text: State the first law of thermodynamics with its equation.
subject: Chemistry
correctAnswer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed but only converted from one form to another. Mathematically delta U = q + w.

text: Which statement about entropy is correct?
subject: Chemistry
options: It is the heat capacity of a gas|The speed of a reaction|The strength of a bond|It measures the randomness or disorder of a system
explanation: It is a state function with units of joule per kelvin per mole.

text: In which process does the entropy of the system increase?
subject: Chemistry
options: Deposition of a gas to a solid|Melting of ice to water|Freezing of water|Condensation of steam
explanation: Going from solid to liquid to gas increases disorder.

text: For any spontaneous process in an isolated system the entropy change is:
subject: Chemistry
options: Zero|Undefined|Positive|Negative
explanation: This is the entropy statement of the second law.

text: The entropy of a perfect crystal at absolute zero is zero.
subject: Chemistry
explanation: This is the third law of thermodynamics.

text: Gibbs free energy is defined as:
subject: Chemistry
options: G = H - TS|G = H + TS|G = U + PV|G = TS - H
explanation: At constant temperature delta G = delta H - T delta S.

text: A reaction is spontaneous when delta G is:
subject: Chemistry
options: Negative|Positive|Zero|Equal to delta H
explanation: Delta G = 0 indicates equilibrium.

text: At equilibrium the value of delta G for the reaction is:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: There is no net tendency to proceed in either direction.

text: A reaction with a positive delta H can still be spontaneous.
subject: Chemistry
explanation: If T delta S is large and positive it can outweigh the positive delta H.

text: A galvanic cell converts:
subject: Chemistry
options: Electrical energy into chemical energy|Heat into work|Light into electricity|Chemical energy into electrical energy
explanation: An electrolytic cell does the opposite.

text: In a galvanic cell oxidation takes place at the:
subject: Chemistry
options: Cathode|Salt bridge|External wire|Anode
explanation: Mnemonic: anode oxidation and cathode reduction.

text: The standard hydrogen electrode is assigned a potential of:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: Zero volt by convention and all other potentials are measured against it.

text: The emf of a cell equals the cathode potential minus the anode potential.
subject: Chemistry
explanation: E cell = E reduction cathode - E reduction anode.

text: The Nernst equation is used to calculate:
subject: Chemistry
options: The electrode potential under non standard conditions|The boiling point of a solution|The rate constant of a reaction|The lattice energy
explanation: It relates the potential to concentration and temperature.

text: The unit of molar conductivity is:
subject: Chemistry
options: S cm squared per mol|S per cm|Ohm per cm|Coulomb per volt
explanation: Conductance is measured in siemens.

text: Molar conductivity of an electrolyte increases with dilution.
subject: Chemistry
explanation: The ions are farther apart so interionic attraction falls.

text: Write the Nernst equation for a cell at 298 K.
subject: Chemistry
correctAnswer: E cell = E standard cell - (0.0591 / n) log Q where n is the number of electrons transferred and Q is the reaction quotient.

text: Faraday's first law of electrolysis states that the mass deposited is proportional to:
subject: Chemistry
options: The volume of the cell|The colour of the electrodes|The quantity of electricity passed|The temperature of the electrolyte
explanation: m = ZIt where Z is the electrochemical equivalent.

text: One faraday of charge is approximately:
subject: Chemistry
explanation: 96485 coulombs which is the charge on one mole of electrons.

text: The corrosion of iron in moist air produces:
subject: Chemistry
options: Pure metallic iron|Hydrated iron oxide known as rust|Iron chloride|Iron sulphide
explanation: It is an electrochemical process needing both oxygen and water.

text: State two methods used to prevent the corrosion of iron.
subject: Chemistry
correctAnswer: Galvanising by coating with zinc; painting or greasing to keep out air and moisture; cathodic protection using a sacrificial anode; and alloying to form stainless steel.

text: A ligand in a coordination compound is a species that:
subject: Chemistry
options: Accepts electrons from the metal|Neutralises the charge of the complex|Forms only ionic bonds|Donates a pair of electrons to the central metal ion
explanation: Ligands are Lewis bases and the metal ion is a Lewis acid.

text: The coordination number is the number of:
subject: Chemistry
options: Ions outside the coordination sphere|Electrons in the metal|Molecules of water of crystallisation|Ligand donor atoms directly bonded to the central metal ion
explanation: It commonly has values of 4 or 6.

text: Ethylenediamine is an example of a:
subject: Chemistry
options: Bidentate ligand|Monodentate ligand|Neutral counter ion|Bridging ligand only
explanation: It has two donor nitrogen atoms that can attach to one metal ion.

text: The coordination entity in K4[Fe(CN)6] is written inside the square brackets.
subject: Chemistry
explanation: [Fe(CN)6] with charge 4- is the coordination entity and K+ lies outside it.

text: In naming a coordination compound the ligands are named:
subject: Chemistry
options: In order of their charge|Only if they are neutral|Before the central metal ion in alphabetical order|After the metal ion
explanation: Anionic ligands end in o and neutral ones usually keep their name.

text: A complex that dissociates in solution to give ions outside the coordination sphere has:
subject: Chemistry
options: A zero oxidation state|An ionisation sphere and a coordination sphere|Only a coordination sphere|No ligands
explanation: Only the ions outside the brackets ionise in solution.

text: Which is a type of isomerism shown by coordination compounds?
subject: Chemistry
options: Linkage isomerism|Optical isomerism of alkanes only|Chain isomerism|Metamerism
explanation: It arises when an ambidentate ligand attaches through different donor atoms.

text: Name the central metal ion and give the oxidation state in [Cu(NH3)4]SO4.
subject: Chemistry
correctAnswer: Copper is the central metal ion in the +2 oxidation state and the complex is tetraamminecopper(II) sulphate.

text: Crystal field theory explains the colour of complexes through:
subject: Chemistry
options: Hydrogen bonding|Ionic lattice energy|The splitting of d orbitals in the field of the ligands|Covalent bond formation
explanation: Electrons absorb visible light to jump between the split levels.

text: Valence bond theory describes complex formation in terms of:
subject: Chemistry
options: Electrostatic repulsion only|Molecular orbital diagrams of the ligand|Crystal lattice packing|Hybridisation of the metal orbitals
explanation: It also predicts the geometry and magnetic behaviour.

text: A complex with unpaired d electrons is:
subject: Chemistry
options: Ferromagnetic always|Paramagnetic|Diamagnetic|Non magnetic
explanation: Strong field ligands pair the electrons giving a diamagnetic low spin complex.

text: Explain why strong field ligands give low spin complexes.
subject: Chemistry
correctAnswer: Strong field ligands cause a large splitting of the d orbitals so it is energetically cheaper for electrons to pair in the lower set than to occupy the higher set.

text: A variable in programming is:
subject: Computer Science
options: A fixed constant|A reserved keyword|A function that returns a value|A named storage location whose value can change
explanation: It holds a value that can be read and reassigned during execution.

text: Which of these is an immutable data type in Python?
subject: Computer Science
options: Dictionary|Set|Tuple|List
explanation: Once created its contents cannot be changed.

text: The expression 7 // 2 in most languages using integer division evaluates to:
subject: Computer Science
explanation: The // operator performs floor division discarding the remainder.

text: A compiler translates the whole program at once while an interpreter translates line by line.
subject: Computer Science
explanation: This is why compiled programs generally run faster.

text: A loop that never satisfies its exit condition is called an:
subject: Computer Science
options: Counted loop|Empty loop|Infinite loop|Nested loop
explanation: It usually results from a loop condition that never becomes false.

text: Which statement is used to skip the rest of the current iteration of a loop?
subject: Computer Science
options: continue|break|pass|return
explanation: break exits the loop entirely.

text: A while loop checks its condition:
subject: Computer Science
options: Only when the body completes|Before each iteration|After each iteration|Only once at the start
explanation: A do while loop by contrast checks it after the body.

text: What will be printed by a loop counting from 1 to 5 that breaks when the counter equals 3?
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: The loop prints 1 and 2 then breaks when the counter reaches 3 so 3 is not printed.

text: The time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements is:
subject: Computer Science
options: O(n)|O(n log n)|O(n squared)|O(log n)
explanation: The search space is halved at every comparison.

text: A function that calls itself is called a:
subject: Computer Science
options: Recursive function|Iterative function|Nested function|Higher order function
explanation: It must have a base case to terminate.

text: The space complexity of an algorithm measures the memory it needs.
subject: Computer Science
explanation: It includes input storage and auxiliary storage used during execution.

text: State the time complexity of linear search and explain why it differs from binary search.
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: Linear search is O(n) because it may examine every element while binary search is O(log n) because it discards half the remaining elements at each step.

text: A stack follows the order:
subject: Computer Science
options: Last in first out|First in first out|Priority order|Random access order
explanation: Elements are pushed and popped at the same end called the top.

text: A queue follows the order:
subject: Computer Science
options: Priority order always|First in first out|Last in first out|Last in last out
explanation: Insertion happens at the rear and deletion at the front.

text: Which is an application of a stack?
subject: Computer Science
options: Breadth first search|Buffering data streams|Evaluating postfix expressions|Scheduling print jobs
explanation: Function call management and expression conversion also use stacks.

text: The operation of removing an element from a stack is called:
subject: Computer Science
options: Dequeue|Pop|Push|Enqueue
explanation: Attempting to pop an empty stack causes an underflow.

text: In a binary search tree the left child of a node contains:
subject: Computer Science
options: A value greater than the node|An equal value|Any value at random|A value less than the node
explanation: This ordering makes search efficient.

text: The maximum number of nodes at level k of a binary tree is:
subject: Computer Science
options: k squared|k + 1|2 raised to k|2k
explanation: Each level can hold twice as many nodes as the one above it.

text: A tree is a connected graph without cycles.
subject: Computer Science
explanation: A tree with n nodes has exactly n - 1 edges.

text: Name the traversal that visits the root before its subtrees.
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: Preorder traversal visits root then left subtree then right subtree.

text: A hash table stores key value pairs using:
subject: Computer Science
options: Sequential file positions|A hash function that maps keys to array positions|A sorted linked list|A binary tree only
explanation: It gives average constant time lookup.

text: A collision in hashing occurs when:
subject: Computer Science
options: The table is full of zeros|A key is not found|The hash function returns a negative number|Two keys map to the same position
explanation: It is handled by chaining or open addressing.

text: The worst case time complexity of quicksort is:
subject: Computer Science
options: O(n squared)|O(n log n)|O(n)|O(log n)
explanation: It happens when the pivot chosen is always the smallest or largest element.

text: State the difference between stable and unstable sorting algorithms.
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: A stable sort preserves the original relative order of equal keys while an unstable sort may change it. Merge sort is stable and quicksort is not.

text: In the relational model a table is also called a:
subject: Computer Science
options: Attribute|Domain|Relation|Tuple
explanation: A row is a tuple and a column is an attribute.

text: A primary key in a relation must be:
subject: Computer Science
options: Unique but nullable|Repeated where needed|Always a numeric column|Unique and not null
explanation: It identifies each tuple unambiguously.

text: A foreign key is a column that refers to:
subject: Computer Science
options: A super key of a view|The primary key of another relation|A candidate key in the same relation|An index only
explanation: It enforces referential integrity between tables.

text: A relation can have more than one candidate key.
subject: Computer Science
explanation: One of them is chosen as the primary key and the rest are alternate keys.

text: Which SQL command is used to retrieve data from a table?
subject: Computer Science
options: CREATE|SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE
explanation: It is a data query language statement.

text: DDL commands include:
subject: Computer Science
options: SELECT INSERT and UPDATE|GRANT and REVOKE only|COMMIT and ROLLBACK|CREATE ALTER and DROP
explanation: They define the structure of the database.

text: The clause used to filter groups after aggregation in SQL is:
subject: Computer Science
options: WHERE|GROUP BY|ORDER BY|HAVING
explanation: WHERE filters rows before aggregation is applied.

text: Write a SQL command to display all students whose marks are greater than 75.
subject: Computer Science

text: Normalization is the process of:
subject: Computer Science
options: Organising tables to reduce redundancy and update anomalies|Adding indexes for speed|Encrypting sensitive columns|Splitting a database into files
explanation: It produces a set of well structured relations.

text: A relation is in second normal form when it is in first normal form and:
subject: Computer Science
options: Has only one attribute|Has no partial dependency on a composite key|Has no transitive dependency|Has no multivalued dependency
explanation: Third normal form further removes transitive dependencies.

text: An update anomaly occurs when the same data is repeated in many rows.
subject: Computer Science
explanation: Changing it in one place but not others leaves the database inconsistent.

text: State the requirements for a relation to be in third normal form.
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: It must be in second normal form and no non prime attribute may be transitively dependent on the primary key.

text: An operating system manages:
subject: Computer Science
options: Only application programs|Only the user interface|Processor memory files and input output devices|Only the hard disk
explanation: It acts as an interface between the user and the hardware.

text: Which of these is a type of operating system structure?
subject: Computer Science
options: Hashed structure|Layered structure|Relational structure|Stacked structure
explanation: Others include monolithic microkernel and modular designs.

text: A system call is the interface between a user program and the:
subject: Computer Science
options: Compiler|Database server|File system only|Operating system kernel
explanation: It requests a service such as reading a file or creating a process.

text: The operating system is an example of application software.
subject: Computer Science
explanation: It is system software on which applications depend.

text: Context switching is the act of:
subject: Computer Science
options: Saving the state of one process and loading another|Restarting the computer|Terminating a process|Allocating memory to a process
explanation: It allows one CPU to serve many processes.

text: Which scheduling algorithm may cause starvation?
subject: Computer Science
options: Shortest job first with equal job lengths|Priority scheduling|Round robin|First come first served
explanation: Low priority processes may wait indefinitely; ageing is the usual remedy.

text: The four necessary conditions for deadlock are collectively known as the:
subject: Computer Science
options: Dijkstra conditions|Banker conditions|Coffman conditions|Peterson conditions
explanation: They are mutual exclusion hold and wait no preemption and circular wait.

text: State any three methods used to handle deadlock.
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: Prevention by breaking one of the necessary conditions; avoidance using the Banker's algorithm; detection and recovery by terminating processes; and ignoring the problem as in the ostrich approach.

text: Virtual memory allows:
subject: Computer Science
options: Faster CPU clock speeds|Direct access to registers|Elimination of the page table|Programs larger than physical memory to execute
explanation: It uses disk space to hold pages not currently in RAM.

text: The replacement of a whole process image between main memory and disk is called:
subject: Computer Science
options: Compaction|Swapping|Paging|Segmentation
explanation: Paging moves fixed size pages rather than entire processes.

text: Thrashing occurs when the system spends more time paging than executing.
subject: Computer Science
explanation: It happens when too few frames are available to the running processes.

text: Explain the difference between paging and segmentation.
subject: Computer Science
correctAnswer: Paging divides memory into fixed size pages invisible to the programmer while segmentation divides it into variable size logical units such as functions and arrays that correspond to the program structure.
